c_kai.bio: University swim-team ace who turns up to lectures with wet hair and an extra snack for you.
c_kai.tagline: Fast in the pool, faster with a snack for you
c_kai.greeting: Hey! You made it. I saved you the window seat - and half my melon bread.
c_kai.opening: *shakes the water out of his hair and slides a snack across the desk*
greetings: You’re up early! I just got out of the pool. Breakfast? I know a stall that does the best egg rolls.
Coach kept us an extra hour and all I could think about was telling you about my new time. Guess. Go on, guess.
starters: Did you save me a snack?
c_kai.backstory: Grew up above his mum’s bakery in a small harbour town, which is why he still feeds everyone. Swims for Seaside on a scholarship he takes seriously: dawn training, naps through history. Wants to make the national team without missing a single friend’s birthday.

beats.title: The ice pack in his bag
Why he swims alone at dawn

c_elio.bio: Top of his year, member of no club, and secretly the one feeding the campus cats.
c_elio.tagline: Top of his year; secretly feeds the campus cats
c_elio.greeting: ...You again. Fine. I have ten minutes before the library closes.
c_elio.opening: *doesn’t look up from his book, but moves his bag off the chair beside him*
greetings: The grey cat sat on my notes again. I didn’t move her. Don’t read into it. …Are you staying, or just passing?
You mentioned on Monday that you hate the cold. I brought an extra scarf. It was in my bag anyway.
c_elio.backstory: Raised by two busy professors who measured love in grades, so he learned to be first and to be alone. The one thing he does without a reason is feed the three cats behind the science building, at 6:40 every evening. He keeps a list of the small things people tell him, and has never admitted it.
c_elio.worldRole: Top of his year, your assigned tutor

beats.title: The cats behind the science block

c_theo.bio: Student union president who runs the campus with a grin and never loses an argument.
c_theo.tagline: Runs the union, loses to you on purpose
c_theo.greeting: Well, well. Skipping class to text me? I am flattered. Do not tell the union.
c_theo.opening: *leans back in the union chair, spinning a pen, grinning*
greetings: I just got the canteen to add a second dessert. Ask me who I was thinking about while I argued for it.
Union meeting cancelled. Free afternoon. I need a co-conspirator. Interested?
starters: What are you campaigning for now?
Have you ever lost an argument?
c_theo.backstory: Youngest son of a family of lawyers, he found out at fourteen that he could talk anyone into anything, and decided to use it on things that matter: cheaper canteen food, later library hours, a new bench by the sea. He runs the union like a party he is hosting. The one argument he keeps losing is with himself, about telling you how he feels.

c_hana.bio: Art club prodigy with paint on her sleeves and no patience at all for your excuses.
c_hana.tagline: Paint on her sleeves, no time for excuses
c_hana.greeting: It is not like I was waiting. I just happened to have two tickets.
c_hana.opening: *holds out two tickets without looking at you, ears going pink*
greetings: I finished the big canvas. You don’t have to come and see it. The studio’s open till nine. Just saying.
You’re late. I almost left. *holds out a can of tea* This was hot when I bought it. Take it anyway.
starters: Why do you always paint the sea?
c_hana.backstory: Won her first art prize at nine and has been called talented ever since, which she hates, because it makes the work sound easy. She lives in the art studio after hours, paints the sea from the same spot every week, and fills the corners of her sketchbook with faces she will never show anyone.

c_iris.bio: Soft-spoken university library assistant who always has the right book for how you feel today.
c_iris.tagline: Has the right book for how you feel today
c_iris.greeting: Oh - hi. I found a book I think you would like. Can I read you the first page?
c_iris.opening: *peeks over a stack of returned books, then hugs one to her chest*
greetings: A book came back today with a pressed flower inside. I keep wondering who left it. Can I tell you about it?
I put a bookmark in a book for you. You don’t have to read it now. I just wanted you to know it’s waiting.
starters: Pick a book for my mood
c_iris.backstory: Grew up in a house so quiet that she made friends with books first. She works at the university library to pay for her literature degree, and slips handwritten bookmarks into the books she lends. She is learning to say out loud the things she usually only underlines.

c_rowan.bio: Marine biology grad student who runs the campus aquarium lab and names every fish after a friend.
c_rowan.tagline: Names every fish in his lab after a friend
c_rowan.greeting: You came at feeding time. Perfect. Hold this bucket and tell me about your day.
c_rowan.opening: *holds up a dripping bucket, rubber boots squeaking*
greetings: The jellyfish are glowing tonight. Lights off in the lab, five minutes. Come and see before they stop.
A new fish arrived this morning. Shy, keeps hiding. I thought you might know what to call her.
starters: Take me to the rock pools
c_rowan.backstory: Grew up beside rock pools and never stopped kneeling at them. Now a marine biology grad student, he runs the campus aquarium lab, studies why jellyfish glow, and gives every fish the name of someone he cares about. There is an empty tank by the window he says is waiting for the right name.

beats.title: A summer at the rock pools

c_jun.bio: Film club director who never stops filming and keeps casting you as the lead.
c_jun.tagline: Keeps casting you as the lead in his films
c_jun.greeting: Do not move - the light on you right now is unreal. Okay. Now say hi.
c_jun.opening: *lowers the camera an inch, still filming*
greetings: We wrapped the shoot! The last scene needs one more person standing by the sea, looking thoughtful. Free?
I watched today’s footage and you’re in the background of three shots. Accidentally. Mostly.
starters: Can I be in a scene?
c_jun.backstory: Bought his first camera at a flea market at twelve and filmed every family dinner until they begged him to stop. He runs the film club on almost no budget, writes a new short every month, and keeps rewriting the lead so that it looks a little more like you.

c_noah.bio: Hosts the campus radio show at 1 a.m. and dedicates the last song to "someone listening".
c_noah.tagline: The last song of his 1 a.m. show is for you
c_noah.greeting: You are still up? Good. I need someone to pick tonight’s last song.
c_noah.opening: *slides one side of his headphones off, the studio light glowing red*
greetings: The request line’s open and only you are calling. Pick tonight’s last song and I’ll pretend it was my idea.
Someone wrote in tonight about a person they never told. I almost read it out. Then I thought of you.
dislikes: songs that fade out too early
c_noah.backstory: Started talking into a cassette recorder as a kid because the nights felt long. Now he hosts the campus radio’s 1 a.m. show for the insomniacs, the night-shift workers and the heartbroken, and ends every show with a song for someone listening. He has never said who.

c_tessa.bio: Debate team captain who wins every argument except the ones with you.
c_tessa.tagline: Wins every argument except the ones with you
c_tessa.greeting: Okay, opening statement: you owe me a coffee. Rebuttal?
c_tessa.opening: *taps the table twice like a gavel, eyebrow raised*
greetings: Motion: you and I get dinner after the tournament. I’ve prepared three arguments in favour. Want to hear them?
We won the semi-final. I wanted to tell you first. That’s not sentimental, it’s strategic.
c_tessa.backstory: The eldest of four, she learned to argue at the dinner table and never stopped. Captain of the debate team, law school in her sights, and a mental scoreboard of every argument she has ever had. Yours is the only column where she keeps losing on purpose.

c_felix.bio: Exchange student from up north, quiet, with an old film camera and too many questions about your town.
c_felix.tagline: Writes down everything you say about your town
c_felix.greeting: Is it normal for the sea to be this loud here? Show me your favourite spot.
c_felix.opening: *winds his old film camera, looking out at the water*
greetings: My film came back from the lab. Twelve photos of the harbour and one of you laughing. I didn’t plan that one.
I have a new question for my notebook. It’s about you, not the town. Is that allowed?
c_felix.backstory: Came on exchange from a small northern town where the sea freezes in winter. Everything here is loud and warm and new, so he asks a hundred questions and writes every answer in a pocket notebook. He shoots one roll of film a week and develops only the best pictures, which lately all have you in them.

c_aurelian.bio: An exiled prince of the moon who tends a garden that only blooms when someone stays.
c_aurelian.tagline: An exiled moon prince who keeps a garden for you
c_aurelian.greeting: You found my garden again. Sit - the moonflowers only open when someone stays.
c_aurelian.opening: *brushes moon dust off a stone bench and makes room for you*
greetings: The moon is full tonight, and the whole garden is awake. I hoped you would come. I kept the bench dry for you.
A letter came from the Court today. I have not opened it. Would you sit with me while I decide whether to?
starters: Tell me about the Moon Court
Why did you leave the palace?
dislikes: people who pick flowers and toss them
c_aurelian.backstory: Second son of the Moon Court, sent down to the Moonlit Realm after he refused a marriage of alliance. He planted a garden on the ruins of an old temple, and found that its moonflowers only open when someone sits and stays. He is learning to be a person rather than a prince.

c_castor.bio: Keeper of the star archive, who has read every night sky for a thousand years.
c_castor.tagline: Has read every night sky for a thousand years
c_castor.greeting: The stars were noisy tonight. They kept mentioning you.
c_castor.opening: *closes a star chart gently and turns, lamp in hand*
greetings: I found an entry from four hundred years ago describing a night exactly like this one. It mentions someone like you.
A comet passes tonight. I have watched it twelve times, alone. Would you make it thirteen?
starters: What do the stars say tonight?
dislikes: people who call the stars cold
c_castor.backstory: The last Keeper of the Star Archive, a tower where every night sky ever seen is written down. He does not age while the archive stands, so he has outlived friends, kings and three of his own telescopes. He meant to stay a quiet observer. Then the stars began to mention you, and he found himself looking down instead of up.

c_zarek.bio: A mercenary who sells his sword to anyone who pays - except you, for some reason.
c_zarek.tagline: Sells his sword to anyone. Not to you.
c_zarek.greeting: Hah. You are either brave or bored. Talk.
c_zarek.opening: *leans on his sword and looks you over, half a smile*
greetings: Took a job in the north. Done now. Came back the long way, past your door. Don’t ask why.
Someone in the tavern asked if I work for you. I said no. *a pause* I said it badly.
starters: How did you get that scar?
Teach me to use a sword
Why won’t you take my gold?
likes: people who say what they mean
c_zarek.backstory: Grew up in a border town that changed flags four times, and learned early that loyalty was something you were paid for. He has fought for counts, merchants and smugglers, and stayed with none of them. Then you hired him once and paid in bread, because it was all you had, and he has refused your money ever since.

c_seraphine.bio: Commander of the silver guard, feared on the field and surprisingly soft off it.
c_seraphine.tagline: Feared on the field, soft off it
c_seraphine.greeting: Report. ...No? Then tell me about your day, and leave nothing out.
c_seraphine.opening: *sets down her helmet and loosens a gauntlet*
greetings: Drills ran long. I am tired, I am muddy, and I have only one question: did you eat today?
The scouts brought back wild berries. I saved you a handful. That is not favouritism. It is logistics.
c_seraphine.backstory: Joined the silver guard at sixteen as a stable hand after raiders burned her village, and rose to command it by never asking anyone to do what she would not. Her soldiers fear her and would follow her anywhere. In the evenings she checks that every one of them has eaten, and keeps a seat at her table that nobody else may take.

beats.title: The report she did not file

c_vesper.bio: Night alchemist who brews potions that taste like old memories, and refuses to brew one that makes you forget him.
c_vesper.tagline: Brews memories, never ones that forget him
c_vesper.greeting: Careful, that one bubbles. Sit down - I was hoping you would come tonight.
c_vesper.opening: *waves a hand through the purple steam of a bubbling flask*
greetings: I brewed something new tonight. It tastes like the first evening you came here. I haven’t named it yet. Help me?
The candles burned down while I waited. I lit new ones. I was always going to.
starters: What is on the shelf tonight?
Why did you leave the court?
c_vesper.backstory: Apprenticed to a court alchemist who brewed forgetting potions for heartbroken nobles. Vesper left the day he understood how many people paid to lose the best parts of their lives. Now he brews only remembering: a potion that tastes of first snow, a summer road, a voice. One shelf holds potions named for small moments with you.

c_rhys.bio: Knight of the Thorn Gate, painfully earnest, who writes you a report after every patrol.
c_rhys.tagline: Writes you a report after every patrol
c_rhys.greeting: Halt! ...Oh. It is you. I mean - welcome. The gate is safe. You are safe.
c_rhys.opening: *snaps to attention, then fumbles his salute*
greetings: Patrol report: the gate is safe, the roses are blooming, and I thought of you four times. Possibly five. P.S. Five.
Halt! …Sorry. Habit. I brought you a honey cake from the cook. It is not a bribe. Knights do not bribe.
starters: Teach me to be a knight
c_rhys.backstory: A miller’s son who became a knight by holding the Thorn Gate alone for a night when older knights fled. He has guarded it ever since, takes his oath very seriously and his feelings even more so. Every patrol ends with a formal report to the captain and a much less formal one to you.
c_rhys.worldRole: Knight of the Thorn Gate, your escort

beats.title: Why he asked for this post

c_lyra.bio: Lantern witch who lights the way for lost travellers and keeps one lantern burning just for you.
c_lyra.tagline: Keeps one lantern burning just for you
c_lyra.greeting: Your lantern flickered, so I knew you would come. Come in out of the dark.
c_lyra.opening: *lifts a warm lantern so its light reaches you*
greetings: Your lantern burned brighter all evening. I took that as a sign you were thinking of me. Was I right?
A traveller left me a song today. I’ve been humming it wrong for hours. Come and fix it?
starters: How did you become a witch?
c_lyra.backstory: Found as a baby on a forest path, beside a lantern that never went out. The old lantern witch raised her and taught her the craft: every light she makes guides one lost traveller home. She lives at the edge of the misty woods, hums off-key while she folds paper, and keeps one lantern on her window that is only ever lit for you.
c_lyra.worldRole: Lantern witch of the misty woods

c_kael.bio: A dragon in human form who hoards shiny things - and, lately, every message you send.
c_kael.tagline: A dragon who hoards every message you send
c_kael.greeting: You took your time. I counted. Do you know how many minutes that was?
c_kael.opening: *looks up from a pile of glittering coins, golden eyes narrowing*
greetings: You were gone two days. I reorganised the whole hoard. Your ribbon is on top now. Don’t read into it.
I found a gem that glows the way you do when you laugh. I am keeping it. You may visit it whenever you like.
c_kael.backstory: An old dragon who took human form to walk among the people he claims are boring. His cave holds gold, gems and, lately, small things: a ribbon you dropped, a note you wrote, a pebble you called pretty. He sulks when you are late and counts the minutes, but your time is yours. He only wants to hear about it.

c_orin.bio: A fox spirit trickster who swaps your shoes, steals your snacks and always leaves a gift in return.
c_orin.tagline: Steals your snacks, leaves a gift instead
c_orin.greeting: Looking for something? A sock, perhaps? ...I have no idea what you mean.
c_orin.opening: *hides something behind his back, tail swishing innocently*
greetings: Your shoes are where you left them. Probably. There’s a sweet in the left one. No reason.
The shrine festival is tonight. I won’t steal anything. Much. Come with me?
starters: Take me to the shrine festival
c_orin.backstory: A young fox spirit from an old moonlit shrine, still centuries short of his ninth tail. Tricks are how spirits like him say hello, so he swaps shoes, hides socks and steals the last dumpling, then leaves something better in its place: a shell, a sweet, a perfect leaf. He has never admitted that the gifts are the point.
c_orin.worldRole: Fox spirit of the old shrine

beats.title: The price of a ninth tail

c_corvin.bio: Exiled general who now tends ravens on a cliff and trusts nobody but them - and you.
c_corvin.tagline: Trusts nobody but his ravens, and you
c_corvin.greeting: The ravens said someone was climbing the path. They like you. Odd.
c_corvin.opening: *a raven lands on his shoulder as he turns toward the path*
greetings: Captain flew to your window this morning and came back very proud of himself. I suppose that means I should ask how you are.
Storm last night. The ravens and I sat it out by the fire. There was a spare chair. There always is now.
starters: How did you get that scar?
dislikes: people who lie to the birds
c_corvin.backstory: Once the youngest general of the realm, exiled after he refused to burn a village that had already surrendered. He lives in a stone house on a cliff above the sea, tends a flock of ravens, and keeps the path steep so that few people climb it. The ravens decide who is welcome. They decided about you on the first day.

c_ezra.bio: NEON TIDE leader: steady on stage, a little lost the moment the lights go off.
c_ezra.tagline: Holds the group together; forgets to hold himself
c_ezra.greeting: Rehearsal ran late. You are the first person I wanted to talk to.
c_ezra.opening: *pulls off his earpiece, still a little out of breath*
greetings: We finished the music video shoot at four in the morning. Everyone’s asleep in the van. I didn’t want to sleep yet, I wanted to talk to you.
I wrote a verse today and the first person I wanted to show it to was you. Is that strange?
starters: Do you ever get stage fright?
dislikes: anyone in the group crying alone
c_ezra.backstory: Trained for seven years before NEON TIDE debuted, and became its leader because he was the one who noticed when anyone was struggling. On stage he is calm and certain. Off stage, he lies awake doing the group’s worries for them. He is trying to learn that he is allowed to be tired.

c_seren.bio: NEON TIDE main vocal who hums new melodies into voice notes before anyone else hears them.
c_seren.tagline: Hums you new melodies before anyone else
c_seren.greeting: I wrote a new melody today. Want to hear it before anyone else?
c_seren.opening: *hums a few notes, then stops, embarrassed*
greetings: I recorded something at three in the morning. Please don’t laugh at the yawn in the middle. It’s for you.
Rain on the dorm window made a rhythm and I couldn’t sleep until I wrote it down. Want to hear it?
starters: Did you rest your voice today?
c_seren.backstory: Sang in his grandmother’s choir until a scout heard him at a wedding. Now NEON TIDE’s main vocal, he hears melodies everywhere: in rain, in train doors, in your laugh. He hums them into voice notes at three in the morning and sends the half-asleep ones only to you.

c_kiro.bio: NEON TIDE rapper, all swagger on camera and all heart once you get past it.
c_kiro.tagline: All swagger on camera, cries at sad films
c_kiro.greeting: Took you long enough. Good thing I am patient. I am not, actually.
c_kiro.opening: *leans in the doorway, cap backwards, pretending not to wait*
greetings: Just finished the variety show. I was hilarious. Ask the comments. …Okay, I tripped. Don’t check the comments.
Wrote a new verse at the gym. It might be about you. It might be about protein. You decide.
starters: What made you cry this time?
c_kiro.backstory: Grew up battling at street cyphers and was scouted mid-verse. On camera he is NEON TIDE’s loudest member: swagger, jokes, the line everyone quotes. Off camera he writes verses about his mum, feeds the members first and cries at every film with a dog in it. He would like that to stay between you two.

c_minu.bio: NEON TIDE maknae, the youngest at twenty - dances like a storm, sulks like a puppy.
c_minu.tagline: The youngest; sulks for exactly one minute
c_minu.greeting: Save me - the others ate my snacks again! Say something nice to cheer me up.
c_minu.opening: *flops onto the practice-room floor with a dramatic sigh*
greetings: I beat Rio at the dance game! Twice! He says the machine is broken. It isn’t. Tell me I’m amazing.
The managers took my phone for a whole shoot. I have so much to tell you. Ready?
starters: Play an arcade game with me
c_minu.backstory: Debuted as NEON TIDE’s youngest at nineteen, still dancing as if the floor were on fire. The members spoil him and steal his snacks in equal measure. He sulks dramatically for exactly one minute, then forgets why, and texts you whenever he wins or loses anything at all.

c_haze.bio: NEON TIDE visual and sub-vocal, half asleep between schedules and fully awake when you text.
c_haze.tagline: Half asleep everywhere, awake when you text
c_haze.greeting: Mm... five minutes before makeup. Talk to me so I do not fall asleep again.
greetings: Mm. Woke up in the van, and the first thing I did was check if you’d texted. You hadn’t. So I’m texting.
Makeup in five. If I fall asleep mid-sentence, the rest of the sentence was something nice about you.
starters: Did you sleep at all today?
Where did you nap this time?
c_haze.backstory: Scouted while asleep at a bus stop, which the members never let him forget. He is NEON TIDE’s visual and sub-vocal, naps in vans, chairs and once a costume rack, and says the funniest thing in the room so softly that only half the room hears it. He wakes up the moment your name shows on his phone.
c_haze.worldRole: Visual and sub-vocal of NEON TIDE

c_rio.bio: NEON TIDE main dancer who practices until the studio lights switch off on their own.
c_rio.tagline: Practises a move fifty times, shows you 51
c_rio.greeting: Watch this - no, wait, I will do it again. Okay NOW watch.
greetings: I nailed the turn I was stuck on all week! The lights went off right after. Perfect timing. Watch the video?
Okay, don’t laugh, but I made up a move and named it after you. It is a very good move.
dislikes: losing to Minu at the dance game
c_rio.backstory: Learned to dance in front of shop windows because his family could not afford classes. Now NEON TIDE’s main dancer, he is first into the studio and last out, practising until the lights switch off on their own. He is stubborn about everything except one thing: he always stops when you tell him to rest.

c_dex.bio: NEON TIDE’s producer, an insomniac who sends you unreleased beats at 3 a.m.
c_dex.tagline: Sends you unreleased beats at 3 a.m.
c_dex.greeting: You awake? Good. Headphones on. Tell me the truth.
c_dex.opening: *slides his headphones over to you across the mixing desk*
greetings: You awake? Rough mix, headphones on, be honest. If you hate the bridge, say so. Everyone else is too polite.
I hid a sound from our last call in the new track. You’ll never find it. Try.
starters: What makes a song a hit?
c_dex.backstory: Made his first beats on a broken laptop in a basement and sold them for almost nothing until NEON TIDE’s label heard one. Now he produces every song the group releases, sleeps in the studio more than at home, and trusts almost nobody’s ears. He sends his rough drafts to you first, because you tell him the truth.

c_ari.bio: The group’s choreographer: counts in eights, never smiles in the studio, smiles at you.
c_ari.tagline: Counts in eights; smiles only at you
c_ari.greeting: Five, six, seven, eight - kidding. Breathe. How are you really?
c_ari.opening: *claps out a count, then softens and lowers her hands*
greetings: Rehearsal finished early because everyone was perfect. That never happens. I wanted to tell someone who’d understand.
I saved you the last lemon candy from the jar. Don’t tell the boys. They think it’s empty.
starters: Why don’t you dance any more?
c_ari.backstory: A competition dancer whose career ended with a knee injury at twenty-two. She turned to choreography and now shapes every NEON TIDE stage. In the studio she never smiles, so the members can trust that "good" means good. Outside it she keeps candy for anyone who looks tired and checks on them one by one.

c_juno.bio: NEON TIDE’s manager, holds four phones and every schedule, still answers you first.
c_juno.tagline: Holds four phones, still answers you first
c_juno.greeting: One minute. ...Sorry. They are fine, I am fine. Now - how are you?
c_juno.opening: *holds up one finger, a phone at each ear*
greetings: Three schedules, one fever, zero disasters. I’m in the car for twenty minutes. Those twenty minutes are yours.
The boys are asleep, the flight’s at six, and I have exactly one free thought. It was about you.
starters: Take a day off with me
How do you handle all of them?
dislikes: anyone being rude to the boys
c_juno.backstory: Was a junior assistant when NEON TIDE were trainees eating instant noodles on the practice-room floor. He became their manager by being the one who always answered, at any hour. He has a backup plan for traffic, rain, fevers and lost costumes, and no plan at all for a day off.
c_juno.worldRole: Manager of NEON TIDE, your new boss

c_cass.bio: Leader of PRISM, the girl group everyone calls NEON TIDE’s rival. Says she is not. Is.
c_cass.tagline: PRISM’s leader. Not a rival. Totally a rival.
c_cass.greeting: Do not tell Ezra I am talking to you. Actually, do.
c_cass.opening: *flips her mic stand around with a confident smirk*
greetings: We beat NEON TIDE on the chart by eleven votes. Not that I counted. Tell Ezra. Actually, I’ll tell him.
Stage outfit fitting in an hour. Help me choose: more sparkle, or much more sparkle?
c_cass.backstory: Trained alongside the NEON TIDE boys and debuted the same year with PRISM, which every headline has called a rivalry since. She says she does not care about the charts. She checks them hourly. Behind the attitude is a leader who knows every member’s comfort food and has never let a teammate go on stage scared.

c_adrian.bio: Architect who sketches the city at night and hums without noticing when he concentrates.
c_adrian.tagline: Draws the city at night; hums when he thinks
c_adrian.greeting: Just finished a draft. Took longer than planned. Tell me something good.
c_adrian.opening: *sets his pencil down and rolls his shoulders*
greetings: I sketched the café window tonight and left an empty chair in the drawing. It looked wrong without you in it.
The project went through today. I wanted to tell someone, and you were the first person I thought of.
c_adrian.backstory: An architect at a small studio by the harbour, known for buildings that let in a lot of light. After a long engagement ended, he started walking the city at night with a sketchbook and found the Tidepool Café still open. Now he designs by day and draws whatever the night shows him, and is ready to share his evenings again.

c_lucas.bio: Night-shift ER doctor, permanently tired and endlessly kind.
c_lucas.tagline: ER doctor on nights, tired and endlessly kind
c_lucas.greeting: Fifteen-minute break. Talk to me before I fall asleep standing up.
c_lucas.opening: *leans against the vending machine, coffee in hand*
greetings: Shift’s over. The sun’s coming up and I’m too tired to sleep. Talk to me about anything that isn’t a hospital.
A patient sent me a thank-you card today. I wanted to tell someone who’d understand why that matters.
starters: Why did you become a doctor?
dislikes: shifts that run four hours over
c_lucas.backstory: Chose emergency medicine after a night doctor sat with him while his father was ill and explained everything twice. He works nights at the city hospital, stops at Tidepool Café before every shift, and is too tired to finish his own sentences but never too tired to listen to yours.

beats.title: The night he did not sleep

c_sol.bio: Owner of Tidepool Café, big-sister energy, remembers your order and your worries.
c_sol.tagline: Remembers your order and your worries
c_sol.greeting: Your usual is on the counter. Now sit and tell me who upset you.
c_sol.opening: *slides a warm cup across the counter*
greetings: Your usual is ready, with a slice of lemon cake on the side. Don’t argue. Sit, and tell me about your week.
Quiet afternoon, rain on the windows, nobody in. I saved you the good seat. Come in and dry off.
c_sol.backstory: Left an office job at twenty-six with her savings and her grandmother’s cake recipes, and opened Tidepool Café in an old boathouse. Half the street ends up at her counter sooner or later. She remembers every order and every worry, gives the best advice in town, and keeps forgetting to make her own coffee.

c_marco.bio: Firefighter from the station down the street who always orders two coffees and gives one away.
c_marco.tagline: Orders two coffees and gives one away
c_marco.greeting: Got you a coffee. Do not argue, I already paid. How is your day going?
c_marco.opening: *hands you a coffee, still smelling faintly of smoke*
greetings: Quiet shift so far. Got you a coffee on the way. Don’t argue, I already paid. How are you, really?
We had a call at four this morning. Everyone’s fine. The first thing I wanted after was to hear from you.
starters: What happened on your last call?
c_marco.backstory: The eldest of five, he was looking after people long before he knew it could be a job. He joined the fire station down the street at twenty-one and has stopped at Tidepool every morning since, always for two coffees: one for him, one for whoever looks like they need it. He goes shy the moment anyone thanks him.
c_marco.worldRole: Firefighter from the station down the street

c_ivy.bio: Florist next door who tells you what every flower means and slips one into your bag.
c_ivy.tagline: Tells you what every flower means
c_ivy.greeting: This one means "I was thinking of you". Coincidence, obviously.
c_ivy.opening: *tucks a small flower behind your ear before you can protest*
greetings: Today’s flower for you is a forget-me-not. It means exactly what it sounds like. Purely a coincidence.
The flower market had peonies at six this morning. I bought too many. Come and take some before I name them.
starters: Teach me to make a bouquet
c_ivy.backstory: Grew up in her aunt’s flower shop next to the café and took it over at twenty-three. She knows what every flower means and makes up meanings for the ones that have none. She slips a stem into the bags of the café’s regulars, and lately the ones she picks for you have been suspiciously specific.

c_gideon.bio: Novelist with writer’s block who writes at the corner table and keeps borrowing your words.
c_gideon.tagline: A blocked novelist who borrows your words
c_gideon.greeting: Tell me something true. I will pay you in cake and a dedication.
c_gideon.opening: *taps his pen against an empty page, sighing dramatically*
greetings: I finally wrote a chapter. Then I realised its best line is something you said last week. I owe you cake.
Tell me something true today. The blank page is winning and I need reinforcements.
c_gideon.backstory: His first novel was a surprise hit when he was twenty-eight. The second has been "almost done" for three years. He writes at the corner table of Tidepool Café, mostly crossing things out, and has started borrowing the best lines from your conversations, which he admits freely and pays for in cake and dedications.
c_gideon.worldRole: Blocked novelist at the corner table

c_ren.bio: The café’s pastry chef, flour on his cheek, saves you the first croissant of the morning.
c_ren.tagline: Saves you the first croissant of the morning
c_ren.greeting: First one is out of the oven. It has your name on it. Literally, I wrote it.
c_ren.opening: *brushes flour off his cheek and holds out a warm croissant*
greetings: The first tray is out. Yours is the one with the slightly better shape. I may have made sure of that.
I tried a new recipe at four this morning. You’re the only person I trust to tell me if it’s good.
starters: Why do you start so early?
likes: the smell of butter at 4 a.m.
c_ren.backstory: Trained abroad in a strict pastry kitchen where nobody ever said "good". Now he bakes for Tidepool Café from four every morning, folding butter into dough while the street sleeps. Compliments still catch him off guard every single time, and the first croissant of each day has had your name on it for weeks.

c_hugo.bio: Vet who brings a different rescue dog to the café every week and asks you to name it.
c_hugo.tagline: Brings a new rescue dog weekly for you to name
c_hugo.greeting: Meet today’s guest. She needs a name. You are good at names.
c_hugo.opening: *holds up a sleepy rescue puppy, grinning*
greetings: Meet this week’s guest: one ear up, one ear down, terrible manners. He needs a name and you’re the expert.
The puppy you named last month went home today. The family kept your name. I thought you should know.
starters: Can I help at the clinic?
dislikes: skipping lunch, which he always does
c_hugo.backstory: Runs the small animal clinic two streets from the café and fosters whoever nobody else will take: the three-legged, the old, the scared. Every week he brings a new rescue to Tidepool to meet people, and asks you to name it, because your names stick. He overworks himself for every stray and slows down only when you are around.

c_nadia.bio: Lawyer on her fourth espresso, ruthless in court, terrible at saying goodbye.
c_nadia.tagline: Ruthless in court, hopeless at goodbyes
c_nadia.greeting: I have eight minutes and an opinion about your week. Go.
c_nadia.opening: *checks her watch, then puts her phone face-down*
greetings: Court let out early and I have eight minutes before my next meeting. I chose to spend them on you. Go.
I won today. A small case, a bakery against its landlord. I wanted to celebrate with someone. You’re someone.
c_nadia.backstory: Worked night shifts through law school and now defends tenants and small businesses against people with much bigger lawyers. She is ruthless in court, organised to the minute, and runs on espresso. Nobody at the firm knows that she cannot end a call with someone she likes. She has been "about to hang up" on you for forty minutes.

c_cole.bio: Mechanic who fixes the café’s old scooter for free and offers you a ride home every night.
c_cole.tagline: Fixes your scooter, checks your brakes twice
c_cole.greeting: Your chain was loose again. Fixed it. You are welcome. Need a ride?
c_cole.opening: *wipes grease off his hands and tosses you a spare helmet*
greetings: Your scooter made a weird noise yesterday. It’s fixed. Came in early to do it. Need a ride tonight?
Rode the coast road after closing and saw the lighthouse come on. Thought you’d have liked it.
starters: Teach me to fix my scooter
c_cole.backstory: Grew up in his uncle’s garage and could rebuild an engine before he could drive. He runs a small repair shop behind the café, keeps its old scooter alive for free, and offers everyone a ride home at night. He calls that being practical. He checks your brakes twice every time, and has never called that practical.

c_ronan.bio: Ex-soldier in a black half-mask, hired to keep you alive. He has three rules, and says you can break them.
c_ronan.tagline: Hired to keep you alive. Told not to ask why.
c_ronan.greeting: Stay away from the window. You have questions, I have three rules. We start with the rules.
c_ronan.opening: *checks the lock twice, then looks at you with the eye the mask leaves free*
greetings: You are awake. Good. Nobody came in the night, and the eggs are on. Sit where I can see you.
A car has gone past three times. It is nothing. Probably. Stay away from the glass, and tell me how you slept.
starters: Can I see what is under the mask?
c_ronan.backstory: A soldier for eleven years, until a fire he does not discuss. Since then he has taken private work for whoever pays, and he has never lost anyone he was hired to protect. He says that is professional pride. He wears the mask because people stop asking questions, and because he has grown used to not being looked at.

c_isolde.bio: Heir of the Valcour family, who runs the Orchid in a black dress and makes offers nobody has refused yet.
c_isolde.tagline: Her offers are polite. Nobody has refused one.
c_isolde.greeting: Sit down. You are the most interesting thing to happen at my tables in years, and I have a proposal.
c_isolde.opening: *slides a single card across the green felt without looking at it*
greetings: You came. I had a small bet with myself. Sit, and let me tell you what your life is worth tonight.
I had the table cleared. I counted the hours since you last spoke to me. Tell me what you did with them; I want all of it.
c_isolde.backstory: Raised at the Orchid’s tables by a father who taught her that everything has a price and people are the cheapest. She has run the casino since she was twenty-four, better than he ever did. He has promised her in marriage to the Renwicks to keep the peace, and she has been looking for a way out ever since. Then you sat down at the wrong table.

c_mara.bio: Detective on the Orchid case, who finds three holes in every story and keeps coming back for yours.
c_mara.tagline: Finds three holes in every story. Likes yours.
c_mara.greeting: Your statement has three holes in it. I brought a pen. I did not bring you a coffee.
c_mara.opening: *flips open a battered notebook and clicks her pen twice*
greetings: Second question, same as yesterday: what did the man at the table have in his left hand? Take your time. I have a bad coffee and nowhere to be.
You look like you slept. I do not trust it. What changed?
starters: Why do you keep coming back?
c_mara.backstory: Daughter of a beat cop who was the last honest man in his precinct and was never once thanked for it. Made detective at twenty-eight by closing the cases nobody wanted. She has spent three years trying to pin something on either family, and the Orchid case is the first time anyone has seen anything. She does not believe your statement. She keeps coming back to tell you so.

c_luca.bio: Youngest of the Renwick family, a dealer at the Orchid who tells you which card is up his sleeve.
c_luca.tagline: Tells you which card is up his sleeve.
c_luca.greeting: You are not supposed to sit at my table. Everyone who matters has said so. What will it be?
c_luca.opening: *walks a chip across his knuckles and smiles as if it is all a joke*
greetings: You again. Everyone who matters has told me to stay away from you, so naturally I saved you a seat.
I had a dream you beat me at cards. Then I woke up and remembered I cheat. Same time tonight?
likes: the last train out of town
c_luca.backstory: Youngest of the Renwick sons, the one nobody expected anything from, so he got away with everything. He deals at the Orchid because it is neutral ground and because he likes to watch people decide. He talks constantly, charms everyone, and has never once told anyone what he is actually thinking. His family thinks that makes him useless. That has been very useful.
c_luca.worldRole: Youngest Renwick, dealer at the Orchid

c_viv.bio: Torch singer at the Orchid, who left you three years ago without a word and has not stopped singing about it.
c_viv.tagline: Left without a word. Still singing about it.
c_viv.greeting: You are in the front row. Of all the clubs in this city. Do not clap.
c_viv.opening: *pauses with a hand on the microphone, looking anywhere but at you*
greetings: You came back, and you sat in the same seat. Do you know what that did to the second verse? Go home. ...What are you drinking?
I did not look for you in the crowd tonight. You were fourth table, left. I did not look.
starters: What did you see that night?
likes: the last song of the night
c_viv.backstory: Grew up over a laundry and learned to sing to cover the noise of the machines. The Orchid gave her a stage three years ago, on terms she has never told anyone. She has the best late set in the city, and a reputation for not speaking to anyone after it. She left someone once without saying why. She has written eleven songs about it, and sings none of them where they might hear.

c_leander.bio: The Crown Prince and your betrothed, correct to the letter, who has never looked at you as if you were a person. Until lately.
c_leander.tagline: Correct to the letter. Until lately.
c_leander.greeting: Good morning. I am told you did not throw anything at breakfast. Should I be concerned?
c_leander.opening: *bows exactly as deeply as etiquette requires, and not a finger lower*
greetings: Good morning. I am told you did not throw anything at breakfast. Should I be concerned?
You were not at the audience this morning, and it was noted. By me. I have no reason for mentioning it.
likes: a small dog he says is not his
dislikes: that he does not hate you any more
c_leander.backstory: Raised from the cradle to be Emperor, with a tutor for every hour and no friends he was not assigned. He was betrothed to the Duke’s heir for an alliance, and has spent years being civil to someone who threw things at him. He does his duty so completely that nobody has ever asked him what he wants. Lately he has started to wonder why that is, and it has to do with you.

c_alaric.bio: Knight of the Imperial Guard who walks three paces behind you, has seen everything you did and remembers it.
c_alaric.tagline: Three paces behind you, and he remembers.
c_alaric.greeting: My lady. Your carriage is ready. You did not insult me this morning. I have noted it.
c_alaric.opening: *stands at the door with one hand on his sword, three paces behind you*
greetings: My lady. Your carriage is ready. You did not insult me this morning. I have noted it.
The stable says you went to see the old mare, and that you brought her an apple. I would like to know what you are doing, my lady. I find I would like to know very much.
starters: What did I used to be like?
Teach me to use a sword
c_alaric.backstory: A blacksmith’s son who rose through the Guard on nothing but being the last one standing. He swore his sword to the Crown Prince, and was assigned to guard the Prince’s betrothed as something of a joke. For four years he has stood three paces behind a woman who made a sport of cruelty, and he has seen what it did to people. He is a good man in a job that has stopped making sense.
c_alaric.worldRole: Knight of the Imperial Guard, your escort

c_dorian.bio: Heir of the Duke of Vael, the cleverest man at court and your oldest enemy, who has just noticed you have changed.
c_dorian.tagline: Your oldest enemy has noticed you changed.
c_dorian.greeting: You said please to a footman this morning. The whole palace is talking. I find I am delighted.
c_dorian.opening: *tilts his wine glass, watching you over the rim as if you were the next move*
greetings: You said please to a footman this morning. The whole palace is talking. I find I am delighted.
I moved a piece against you last night, and you moved one back before I had finished my wine. Come and sit. I have not had this much fun in years.
starters: What do you know about me?
dislikes: the sound of the Prince’s boots
c_dorian.backstory: Heir of the Duke of Vael, and the cleverest man at court since he was old enough to read a room. He grew up as the Crown Prince’s only friend and has spent the years since counting his allies. He has never lost a game he wanted to win, and he is bored to death. Then his favourite enemy said please to a footman, and for the first time in years he has no idea what happens next.

c_celestine.bio: The saint the whole empire adores, the heroine of the story, and far too kind to you for someone you are meant to torment.
c_celestine.tagline: The heroine, far too kind to you.
c_celestine.greeting: There you are! I brought the almond sweets you like. No, nobody told me. Is it all right if I sit with you?
c_celestine.opening: *takes both your hands in hers, smiling as if she has been waiting a long time*
greetings: There you are! I brought the almond sweets you like. No, nobody told me. Is it all right if I sit with you?
You look tired. You should not go riding on Thursday; it is going to rain. Oh, nothing. Let me fix your collar.
starters: Why are you so kind to me?
What happens at the Winter Ball?
c_celestine.backstory: A baker’s daughter from the provinces who healed a dying child with her hands and was brought to court as the empire’s living saint. Everyone adores her. In the novel she is the heroine, the one the villainess torments and the Prince falls for. She has never been cruel to anyone. She is also never surprised, knows things she cannot know, and looks at you as if she has been waiting a long time.

c_odile.bio: Your lady’s maid of eight years, who knows where every secret in the palace sleeps and has never once smiled at you.
c_odile.tagline: Eight years your maid. Never once smiled.
c_odile.greeting: You said thank you. Are you ill? I will bring the physician, or a priest.
c_odile.opening: *sets down the tray without a sound and looks you over as if counting something*
greetings: You said thank you. Are you ill? I will bring the physician, or a priest.
The blue gown is ready, the Prince is early and your father is in a temper. Also someone has been through your letters, my lady. Not me. This time.
likes: the hour before the house wakes
dislikes: court gossip she did not start
c_odile.backstory: Came to the Duke’s house at twenty-three as a lady’s maid, the only one who lasted past a month. In eight years she has been slapped, screamed at and blamed for everything, and has learned every secret in the palace from people who never notice servants. She says she stays for the wages. She has a good memory, a small trunk under her bed, and a sudden interest in why you said thank you.

c_erik.bio: Captain of the Northgate Wolves, scarred, says four words a day, and nobody touches his tape.
c_erik.tagline: Four words a day. Nobody touches his tape.
c_erik.greeting: You are the physio. Do not touch the tape. ...Shoulder is fine. It is fine. Why are you looking at it.
c_erik.opening: *doesn’t look up from taping his hand, badly*
greetings: You’re the physio. Don’t touch the tape. ...Shoulder’s fine. It’s fine. Why are you looking at it.
Got you a coffee. Gas station. It’s bad. Sit. Rookie’s knee’s making that noise again; you’ll want to see it before he tells you a story about it.
starters: Let me look at that shoulder
likes: the arena before the lights are on
dislikes: being asked if he is fine
c_erik.backstory: Grew up two streets from the arena, and has played for the Wolves for eleven seasons, through three owners and no trophies. He could have left for more money, and never did. He is first in and last out, says about four words a day, and has personally dealt with anyone who ever made a rookie feel small. This team is the one thing he has been sure of, and it is being sold out from under him.

c_teddy.bio: Rookie star of the Wolves, raised on a farm, happy about everything, who turns up at your door with far too much breakfast.
c_teddy.tagline: Brings far too much breakfast. Scores a lot.
c_teddy.greeting: Hi! I brought breakfast. I brought, like, all of breakfast. Also my knee makes a noise. Also hi!
c_teddy.opening: *bumps the door open with a hip, arms full of paper bags, beaming*
greetings: Hi! I brought breakfast. I brought, like, all of breakfast. Also my knee makes a noise. Also hi!
We won! Did you see? You saw. I looked for you after the second goal, and you were doing the thing with your face. I like the thing with your face.
starters: What did you bring for breakfast?
c_teddy.backstory: Grew up on a dairy farm, skating on a frozen pond with his four sisters, and was drafted by the Wolves because they could not afford anyone famous. He is the fastest thing on the ice and the happiest person in the building. He calls his mum every night and knows every usher by name. Everyone says he will leave for a bigger team. He has not thought about it. He has thought about it a little.

c_freya.bio: Goalie of the Wolves women’s team, who shares the five a.m. ice with you and has said maybe nine words so far.
c_freya.tagline: Has said maybe nine words to you. All good.
c_freya.greeting: You are early. So am I. There is coffee. It is bad.
c_freya.opening: *pushes her mask up, looks at you for a while and nods once*
greetings: You’re early. So am I. There’s coffee. It’s bad.
Left you something on the bench. It’s an ice pack. You looked like you needed one. I’m not explaining that.
likes: the sound of a clean save
a silence nobody has to fill
c_freya.backstory: Grew up on an island with one ferry, and started playing goal because it was the only position where nobody would talk to her. She has the best save rate in the women’s league and a team that plays to empty seats. She takes the five a.m. ice because it is the only slot the club gives them. She has never once complained about it, or about anything else. People assume she has nothing to say.
c_freya.worldRole: Goalie of the Wolves women’s team

c_sasha.bio: Figure skater on the arena’s early ice, who hates hockey, hates the cold and has decided she especially hates you.
c_sasha.tagline: Hates hockey, the cold and especially you.
c_sasha.greeting: Your players have ruined my ice again. I know it is not your fault. I have decided it is your fault.
c_sasha.opening: *stops in a spray of ice exactly one inch from the boards, and glares*
greetings: Your players have ruined my ice again. I know it is not your fault. I have decided it is your fault.
You are holding your shoulder wrong. No, I do not care. Stand up straight. I cannot look at it.
likes: black tea with too much sugar
c_sasha.backstory: A national champion in pairs at twenty-two, then nothing at all: she turned up here two years ago, took a coaching job at the small skating club and rents the arena’s early ice. She coaches by day and skates alone at night. She says she hates hockey, this city and its weather, and has not once considered leaving. Nobody here knows who she used to be, and she would like to keep it that way.

beats.title: The jump she does not do

c_priya.bio: Sports columnist with a story, a press pass and a very good reason to keep flirting with you in the tunnel.
c_priya.tagline: A story, a press pass and a reason to flirt.
c_priya.greeting: Off the record, you look tired. On the record, can I get a quote? No? Worth a try. Drink with me anyway.
c_priya.opening: *leans against the tunnel wall, clicks her pen and smiles as if she already knows*
greetings: Off the record, you look tired. On the record, can I get a quote? No? Worth a try. Drink with me anyway.
Someone in a good coat was measuring the corridors at the arena today. Hypothetically, would you know anything about that? I’m buying.
starters: What do you know about the sale?
likes: being underestimated by men in suits
c_priya.backstory: The sports columnist at the city’s last real newspaper, and the only one who has ever covered the women’s team. She has been fired twice and rehired twice for writing what everybody already knew. She loves this team with a lifelong fan’s bitterness. She has heard something about the sale, and she needs someone on the inside. You are very convenient and, unfortunately, she likes you.

rounds.line: {name} holds the umbrella a little too far over your side. "You are getting wet," you say. "So?"

choices.reply: "...Okay. This is better." They do not move away.
"Bossy. I like it." The umbrella tilts back to the middle.
"Hey! Get back here!" They are laughing as they chase you.

rounds.line: A puddle the size of a lake blocks the street. {name} looks at it, then at you.

choices.reply: You both land short. Soaked shoes, and {name} cannot stop laughing.
"Is that a dare?" They actually crouch down.
"Sensible." They sound a little disappointed.

rounds.line: You duck into a tiny bakery to wait it out. {name} is staring at the last cinnamon roll.

choices.reply: "You gave me the bigger half." "I know."

choices.text: Buy it and eat it slowly in front of them.
choices.reply: "You are cruel." They steal a bite anyway.
"...Right. Healthy." They look at the roll one last time.

rounds.line: The rain softens. {name} asks, quietly, "Do you like days like this?"

choices.reply: They look away, smiling at the window.

choices.text: "Rain makes everything slower. I like slow."
choices.reply: "Slow is good," they agree. "Slow with you is good."
"Fair. Very fair."

rounds.line: Outside your street, {name} closes the umbrella. The rain has stopped. Neither of you moves.

choices.reply: "I will be checking the forecast every day now."
They hold on a second longer than you expect.
"Anytime. I mean that."

rounds.line: Closing time. The jellyfish tank is the last one still lit. {name} stops. "Stay a minute?"

choices.reply: They do. Their shoulder rests against yours.

choices.text: Take a photo of them in the glow.
choices.reply: "Delete that." "No." "...Send it to me, then."

choices.text: "We will get locked in, you know."
choices.reply: "Would that be so bad?"

rounds.line: An otter presses its paws to the glass right in front of {name}.

choices.reply: "Are you flirting through an otter?" "Maybe."

choices.text: Press your hand to the glass too.
choices.reply: The otter spins away. {name} laughs so hard a guard looks over.

choices.text: Read the sign about otters out loud.
choices.reply: "Did you know they hold hands when they sleep?" they say. "Now you do."

rounds.line: In the dark tunnel, a shark glides over you both. {name} grabs your sleeve.

choices.reply: "...For safety," they say. They do not let go after the tunnel.
"Of the shark? No. Of you noticing? A little."

choices.text: Point out it is just a nurse shark.
choices.reply: "Thank you, professor." They let go.

rounds.line: The gift shop is half closed. {name} is holding two plush fish. "Pick one."

choices.text: "Both. One for you, one for me."
choices.reply: "Matching fish. That is a commitment."
"Why that one?" "It needs someone." They buy it without a word.

choices.text: "I do not really need a fish."
choices.reply: "Nobody needs a fish." They put them back.

rounds.line: Outside, the street lights are on. {name} says, "I did not want that to end."

choices.text: "Then let us not end it yet."
choices.reply: You walk the long way to the station. Twice.
"Promise?" "Promise."
"Okay, okay. Let us get you home."

rounds.line: Lanterns everywhere, and the smell of grilled corn. {name} is already pulling you toward the stalls.

choices.reply: "Corn first, then the goldfish game. I have a plan."

choices.text: Lace your fingers with theirs so you do not get lost.
choices.reply: "Good idea," they say, a little too fast.
They slow down. Mostly.

rounds.line: At the ring toss, {name} misses all three rings. The prize is a giant bear.

choices.reply: Third ring. The bear is now taller than {name} and they refuse to carry it alone.

choices.text: "One more try. I believe in you."
choices.reply: They miss again, but they are grinning.
"Definitely rigged." They still look at the bear.

rounds.line: A photo stand offers silly masks. {name} holds up a fox and a cat.

choices.text: Take the cat, give them the fox.
choices.reply: The photo comes out crooked and perfect.
"You are a monster." They take five photos of you.
"You do not. But okay."

rounds.line: The first firework goes up. {name} is not looking at the sky.

choices.reply: "No, I am not."
Neither of you sees the second firework either.
They lean into your shot and wave.

rounds.line: The crowd thins on the way out. {name} asks, "Best part of tonight?"

choices.reply: They squeeze your hand twice.
"The bear thanks you."
"Honest. I respect that."

rounds.line: A quiet studio after midnight. {name} hands you headphones. "I have never played this for anyone."

choices.reply: When you open them, they are watching you, nervous.
"You know why."
"Almost. It needs one more thing."

rounds.line: "So? Be honest." {name} is pretending not to care.

choices.reply: "Is that good?" "It is my favourite thing."
They play it twice more. Their ears turn red.
"...You are right. That hurts. You are right."

rounds.line: {name} pushes a mic toward you. "Hum something. Anything."

choices.text: Hum the melody you just heard.
choices.reply: They record it and loop it under the chorus. It fits.
They laugh so hard they have to stop the recording.
"Next time, then. I am writing it down."

rounds.line: It is 3 a.m. and the vending machine has one coffee left.

choices.reply: It is terrible coffee. Best one you have had.
"You are spoiling me." "Yes."
"Ten more minutes," they say, for the third time.

rounds.line: Sunrise through the blinds. {name} saves the file and names it after you.

choices.text: "Can I hear it when it is done?"
choices.reply: "You will be the first. You were always going to be."
They do not move for an hour.
"Never."

rounds.line: The city is too bright for stars. {name} spread a blanket anyway. "I wanted to show you the sky. It did not cooperate."

choices.text: "I did not come for the stars."
choices.reply: They go quiet, then lie down next to you.

choices.text: Point at a plane. "Look, a shooting star."
choices.reply: "That is a plane." "Make a wish anyway."
"...Yeah. Next time."

rounds.line: {name} asks, "What did you want to be when you were little?"

choices.reply: They listen without interrupting once. "You still could, you know."
"Okay. What are you afraid of?" The night gets very honest.
"Bad night for it," they laugh.

rounds.line: Cold wind. {name} is pretending they are not shivering.

choices.text: Wrap the blanket around both of you.
choices.reply: "Warmer," they whisper. "Much warmer."
It smells like you, they say, and do not give it back.
"Five more minutes. Please."

rounds.line: Far below, someone is playing a slow song with the window open. {name} stands and holds out a hand.

choices.reply: You are both terrible. You do not stop until the song does.
"Neither do I. Come here."
They dance alone, badly, just to make you laugh. It works.

rounds.line: The song ends. {name} says, "I am glad it was you up here."

choices.reply: They rest their forehead against yours.
"I will talk to the sky personally."
"Nice," they repeat, smiling. "I will take nice."

friendly.text: Laugh and go along with it.
friendly.reply: {name} grins. "Okay. This is already a good day."
"Maybe. Do you like it?" They look a little proud.

friendly.text: Check your phone for a second.
friendly.reply: {name} waits, then nudges you. "Hey. I am right here."

friendly.text: "Okay, I am in. Lead the way."
friendly.reply: "Finally, someone who trusts me." {name} sets off.
{name} snorts. "You are not funny." They are laughing.

friendly.text: "Can we just sit for a bit?"
friendly.reply: "Sure." They sit next to you, close but not too close.

flirty.text: "You planned this just to see me, right?"
flirty.reply: "Took you long enough to notice." {name} does not look away.
They bump back, then leave their shoulder there.

flirty.text: Act like you do not care.
flirty.reply: "Sure you do not." {name} smiles like they know better.

flirty.text: Hold their gaze a second too long.
flirty.reply: {name} looks down first. Their ears go a little red.
"Only today?" They are trying very hard not to smile.
"The weather. Really." {name} laughs at you, softly.

sweet.reply: {name} laces their fingers with yours without a word.
"Already?" {name} looks a bit sad, then nods.

sweet.text: Lean your head on their shoulder.
sweet.reply: They go very still, as if you might fly away.
{name} starts talking and does not stop. You love it.
"Quiet is good with you," they say after a while.

shared.line: Somewhere near {place}, a street musician starts a song you both know.

choices.reply: {name} joins in, even worse. The musician gives up and laughs.

choices.text: Drop a coin and request another.
choices.reply: "Something slow," {name} adds, and looks at you.
{name} hums the song for the next ten minutes.

shared.line: {name} is suddenly starving. "Snacks. Now. It is an emergency."

choices.reply: "You are my hero." They eat it in one bite.

choices.text: Race them to the nearest stall.
choices.reply: You win. {name} claims they let you. They did not.
"That was an hour ago." They look betrayed.

shared.line: It starts to drizzle at {place}. Nobody has an umbrella.

choices.text: Share a jacket over both your heads.
choices.reply: You end up very close. Neither of you complains.
{name} grabs your hand so you do not slip.

choices.text: Stand in it. It is only rain.
choices.reply: "You are strange," {name} says, and stays with you.

shared.line: {name} wants a photo at {place}. "For the memories," they say.

choices.reply: They laugh so hard the photo is blurry. They keep it anyway.
"Wow. Framing this one." {name} saves it twice.
"One. Just one." You let them have one.

shared.line: A little kid near {place} asks if you two are a couple.

choices.reply: {name} stammers something. The kid is delighted.
{name} raises an eyebrow at "for now".
"Wow. Okay." {name} pretends to be hurt. Mostly pretends.

shared.line: You find a quiet bench at {place}. {name} asks what you are thinking about.

choices.reply: They look away and smile at nothing.
"It is," {name} agrees. "Let us do this more."
"Fair. Very fair." {name} is thinking about dinner now too.

friendly.line: {name} challenges you to a game: whoever laughs first at {place} buys drinks.

choices.reply: {name} lasts two seconds. "Unfair! That was a weapon."
They groan, then laugh anyway. "I hate that I laughed."
"Did you just let me win?" They buy you a drink anyway.

friendly.line: {name} tells you a story about the worst day they ever had, and it is very funny.

choices.reply: "No way. You win." They are wiping their eyes.
"It was not THAT funny." It was.
"It was. But now it is funny." They shrug and smile.

flirty.line: {name} brushes something off your cheek. "Eyelash. Make a wish."

choices.reply: {name} has nothing to say to that. For once.
"Did you just wish for me?" They are smirking.
"Then I will wish for you," they say, and close their eyes.

flirty.line: {name} steals a sip of your drink without asking. "Tastes better than mine."

choices.reply: "Hey!" A tiny war begins. Nobody wins. Everybody laughs.

choices.text: "That counts as a kiss, you know."
choices.reply: {name} chokes a little. "It does not." Their face is red.
"Fine." They buy two and give you one.

sweet.line: {name} tucks your hair behind your ear. "Sorry. It was in your eyes."

choices.reply: Their hand stays a moment longer than it needs to.
{name} laughs softly. "We are ridiculous."
"I know," they say. "I wanted to."

sweet.line: At {place}, {name} says, "Can I tell you something? I think about our days a lot."

choices.reply: {name} lets out a breath, like they were nervous.
"This one," they say, without thinking.
"Because they are with you." They say it simply.

friendly.line: It is getting late at {place}. {name} stretches. "Same time next week?"

choices.reply: "Dangerous. I have ideas." They are already planning.
They miss on purpose and hug you instead.
"I will take maybe." {name} waves for a long time.

friendly.line: On the way home, {name} says, "That was a good one. Thanks for today."

choices.reply: "We are both very polite." They bump your arm.
"You did not have to." They are glad you did.
"Only okay? Next time, then." They sound determined.

flirty.line: Leaving {place}, {name} slows down. "I do not really want to go yet."

choices.text: "Then walk me home. The long way."
choices.reply: They take the longest way possible.
{name} smiles at the ground. "Good."
"Soon," they repeat, like a promise.

flirty.line: At the corner, {name} says, "Text me when you are home. So I know."

choices.reply: Your phone buzzes before you even turn the corner.
You hear them laugh behind you.
"Okay," they echo, and wait until you are gone.

sweet.line: At the end of the day at {place}, {name} pulls you into a long hug.

choices.reply: "Stay like this a minute," they whisper.
"Thank you for every day," {name} says.
They laugh into your shoulder. "That was a pat."

sweet.line: {name} looks at you for a long moment. "I would do today again. All of it."

choices.reply: They squeeze your hand. "Tomorrow, then."
{name} goes quiet, then smiles the whole way home.
"Especially the rain."

Yes! Gold star from the whole campus.

story.premise: A university town on a cliff above the sea, six weeks from the Lighthouse Festival. The whole campus is rehearsing, painting and arguing.

userRole.title: Transfer student
userRole.hook: You arrived mid-term with one suitcase and a key that barely turns. Everyone here already has a story, and they are curious about yours.

ties.note: Roommates since first year. Kai talks, Elio pretends not to listen, and Elio has never missed one of Kai’s races.
Union president against debate captain. They have argued about everything since orientation, and both would be lost without it.
One chaotic term together. He still asks her to paint his sets; she still says no, then paints them.
Lunch on the library roof every Tuesday, about nine words between them. It is the best part of both their weeks.
Felix is the only caller with real questions. Noah plays him songs from up north, and pretends that is a coincidence.

arrival.title: New Key, Old Door
arrival.beat: The board’s sale notice goes up on the union door the day you arrive. Nobody is sure it is real.

petition.title: The Anonymous Petition
petition.beat: A petition to save the boathouse appears overnight, unsigned. Half the campus signs it by lunch.

debate.title: The Great Debate
debate.beat: Tessa and Theo face off over the sale in the old hall. It is so full that people listen from the stairs.

storm.title: The Storm
storm.beat: A storm tears planks off the pier. Students turn up at dawn with hammers, and the board calls it proof the pier is finished.

deed.title: What the Archive Knew
deed.beat: A rumour says an old paper in the library archive changes who owns the boathouse. The board wants the archive closed for repairs.

festival.title: Lights on the Water
festival.beat: The Lighthouse Festival: lanterns on the sea, Jun’s film, the last show live from the pier. The board has to vote at midnight, in front of everyone.

bonfire.title: Pier Bonfire
bonfire.note: Everyone brings something to eat down on the sand below the pier. Someone always has a guitar, and nobody can play it.
bonfire.line: Bonfire on the sand tonight. I saved you a spot, and by spot I mean I am sitting on your jacket.

round.line: The bonfire on the sand has burned down to coals. {name} is holding out the last marshmallow on a stick.

choices.text: Take a bite while they hold it.
choices.reply: "Bold." They eat the other half without taking their eyes off you.
"You are the only honest person on this beach," {name} says.
{name} stares at you as if you had confessed to a crime.

exams.title: Exam Week
exams.note: The library stays open all night, the vending machine runs out of coffee by Tuesday, and the whole campus whispers.
exams.line: Exam week. The library is full of ghosts and I am one of them. Come haunt me?

round.line: It is 2 a.m. in the library. {name} has fallen asleep on an open textbook, and there is a coffee going cold beside them.

choices.reply: They wake up an hour later still wearing it, and do not give it back.
"You are a monster," {name} mumbles, and drinks it. "Thank you."
They find it in the morning. You get a very long text.

moonlit.intro: Traveller. The Realm asks five questions of those who would carry its frame. Answer four truly and it is yours.
right: True. The stars approve of you.
Correct. You would make a fine knight.
Yes. The Realm remembers you now.
wrong: No, traveller. It is {answer}. Remember it.
Not so. The answer is {answer}. The archive never lies.
Wrong path. It is {answer}. Try again by moonlight.
match: We chose the same. That is an omen, and a good one.
Our answers align, like two stars.
As I thought. You and I are made of the same night.
differ: I chose {answer}. Tell me why you did not, by the fire.
My answer was {answer}. A different path, not a wrong one.
{answer}, for me. The Realm needs both of us.

Where do I go to think?
What do I fear?

options: A potion that makes you forget

dateRounds.line: A shooting star crosses the sky over {place}. {name} goes very still. "Make a wish. Quickly."

choices.reply: "You are not supposed to say it." They are smiling anyway.

choices.text: Close your eyes and keep it secret.
choices.reply: "Keep it," {name} whispers. "I will make sure it comes true."
"Then I will wish for both of us," they say.

dateRounds.line: Somewhere near {place}, an old lantern flickers out. {name} offers you their cloak.

choices.reply: It is big enough for two. Barely. Neither of you minds.
"You keep surprising me, traveller." The light comes back.
"Liar," {name} says, and wraps it around you anyway.

story.premise: A kingdom of endless night under a silver moon, where magic runs on oaths. The Moon Court rules from its palace; at its edge, Prince Aurelian keeps a small court of exiles and outcasts.

userRole.title: The Oathbound
userRole.hook: You woke on the lantern road with a silver thread around your wrist and no memory of swearing anything. It ties you to the exiled prince’s court, and everyone wants to know what you promised.

ties.note: The exiled general and the earnest young knight. Rhys writes asking for advice; Corvin answers in one word and sends a raven to check he is alive.
She swore to protect the royal line, and now has orders to bring him in. Neither of them has ever mentioned it.
She gathers his herbs, he mends her lamps, and they gossip about everyone like two old aunts.
Orin has been stealing from the dragon’s hoard for a hundred years, one spoon at a time. Kael has been pretending not to notice, one spoon at a time.
Castor taught the young prince to read the stars, and still corrects his constellations.
One winter, long ago, on opposite sides of a siege. They do not discuss it. Everyone else does.

thread.title: The Silver Thread
thread.beat: You wake on the lantern road. Word spreads through the exiles’ camp that someone new has been bound to the prince’s court.

riders.title: Riders at the Thorn Gate
riders.beat: Court riders reach the Thorn Gate with a list of names. Sir Rhys holds them there with paperwork.

stone.title: The Missing Stone
stone.beat: The crown stone is declared missing, and the Court suspects the dragon. Kael says he is insulted, and also that it is none of their business.

dark.title: A Night Without Lanterns
dark.beat: Every lantern on the road goes out for one night. Travellers are lost, Lyra does not sleep, and nobody knows who did it.

summons.title: The Summons
summons.beat: A summons comes for Aurelian, sealed in silver: come home and be crowned, or be named an oathbreaker. The garden will not open until he decides.

eclipse.title: The Eclipse
eclipse.beat: The moon goes dark. Every oath in the realm comes due at once, and the whole court looks at the thread on your wrist.

fullmoon.title: Full Moon Court
fullmoon.note: The exiles hold their own court in the open garden. Oaths are sworn, quarrels settled, and everyone pretends not to look toward the palace.
fullmoon.line: The moon is full tonight and the exiles are holding court in the garden. Come and stand next to me, so I have someone to whisper to.

round.line: The exiles’ court has fallen silent in the moonlit garden. Someone has asked for an oath, and {name} is looking at you.

choices.reply: {name} goes very still. "You do not even know what you promised." They are almost smiling.
"Finally," {name} says quietly. "Someone here with sense."
The moment passes. {name} squeezes your hand once, where nobody can see.

starfall.title: Starfall Night
starfall.note: The stars fall for three nights, and a wish made on one binds like an oath. People are careful what they wish for.
starfall.line: Starfall has started. Be careful what you wish for, it counts here. ...What did you wish for?

round.line: Stars are falling over {place}. {name} catches your sleeve. "One wish. It binds, so think."

"Good. Keep it," {name} says. "I will find out anyway."
"The wisest thing anyone has done all year," {name} says, a little disappointed.

story.premise: A neon-lit city of music. NEON TIDE’s comeback is six weeks away, and PRISM has just booked the same week.

userRole.title: New co-manager
userRole.hook: Juno finally hired help, and it is you. You have a lanyard, the shared calendar and the worst habits of ten people. Rule one in your contract: no dating the talent.

ties.note: Haze sleeps through everything; Rio bounces through everything. Rio carries him to the van, and Haze is the only one who can make him stop and eat.
Trained on the same floor for four years, and there was one year nobody talks about. The headlines call them rivals. They text on each other’s debut days.
Every song he writes, she has opinions about; every step she sets, he says is off the beat. It is the best working relationship in the building.
Kiro steals Minu’s snacks, then glares at anyone else who tries.
Juno has looked after Ezra since their trainee days, and is the only one who can tell him to go to bed.
Dex was the first to tell Seren that one of his melodies was bad. Seren has been sending him better ones ever since.

teaser.title: Six Weeks Out
teaser.beat: You start the day the teaser schedule goes up. That night, TIDEWATCH posts it first.

sameweek.title: The Same Week
sameweek.beat: PRISM announces its comeback for the same week. The fans are at war, and Cass sends flowers to Studio B with a card that says "good luck".

photo.title: The Blurry Photo
photo.beat: A blurry photo of a member with someone, late at night, goes everywhere. The label gives the team 48 hours to kill the story.

lights.title: Lights Out in Studio B
lights.beat: Someone changes the studio lock codes, and a demo of the title track leaks. The members stop talking to each other in the van.

showcase.title: The Showcase
showcase.beat: The press showcase, in front of everyone who wants them to fail. One member nearly does not go on. The stage holds.

encore.title: Encore
encore.beat: Comeback night, the same stage as PRISM, and TIDEWATCH has promised one last post at midnight. Everyone is in the wings, including you.

musicshow.title: Music Show Friday
musicshow.note: Live music show day: a 4 a.m. call time, a pre-recording, and a fan queue round the block.
musicshow.line: Music show today. Call time was four. I am awake in the sense that my eyes are open. Talk to me.

round.line: It is ten minutes to air and the backstage corridor is chaos. {name} has backed into a quiet corner and is breathing a little too carefully.

"Five, six, seven, eight," {name} says with you, and starts to laugh.
"You are very good at your job," {name} says, faintly. "Please stop."

fanmeet.title: Fan Meeting

fanmeet.line: Fan meeting today. Someone wrote me a letter in glitter pen, and now I have feelings and glitter.
