story.premise: A small harbour street where everyone knows your order. You have just moved into the flat above Tidepool Café, and the whole street has opinions about it.

userRole.title: The new tenant upstairs
userRole.hook: You signed the lease on the flat above the café without reading it closely. The floor creaks, the kitchen smells of butter by five, and everyone downstairs already knows your name.

ties.note: Cole says about ten words a day; Marco says the rest. They have fixed every broken thing on the street together, and argued about all of it.
Sol hired Ren when nobody else would, and reads his mood by how much butter he uses.
One year, one very bad dinner party. She still handles his contracts and he still dedicates chapters to her, and neither will say why.
She fills his clinic with flowers; he names dogs after her customers. They have a bet on who marries first.
They meet at the same ER more often than either would like, and always end up at the same café after.
He keeps telling her the café’s roof is going to fall in. She keeps telling him she will charge him for saying so.

keys.title: The Flat Upstairs
keys.beat: You move in. There is a letter on the mat from Meridian Holdings, addressed to the last tenant, offering money to leave.

sign.title: The Sign on the Corner
sign.beat: A "coming soon" sign goes up on the corner, with a drawing of a tower. Sol takes it down. It is back by morning.

meeting.title: The Street Meeting
meeting.beat: The whole street crams into the café after closing. Nadia explains the law and Marco makes everyone laugh. Nobody admits who has had an offer.

sold.title: Someone Already Sold
sold.beat: It comes out that one lease on the street was sold months ago. Everyone starts looking at each other differently.

market.title: The Biggest Market
market.beat: The street throws the biggest night market it has ever had, to show the council what would be lost. It rains. Everyone stays.

vote.title: The Council Vote
vote.beat: The council votes on the tower. The street walks there together, and Sol closes the café for the first time in four years.

nightmarket.title: Saturday Night Market
nightmarket.note: Stalls all down the harbour street, string lights, Ren’s pastries, Ivy’s flowers and too much music.
nightmarket.line: Night market tonight. I will be the one pretending I am not looking for you.

round.line: The market is packed and the string lights have just come on. {name} is holding two paper cones of something hot and has clearly bought one for you.

choices.text: Take it, and stay close in the crowd.
choices.reply: Somewhere around the flower stall, your shoulders stop being an accident.
"No idea," {name} says happily. "Very brave of us."
"Fine," {name} says, and eats both, looking at you the whole time.

lights.title: Harbour Lights
lights.note: Every boat in the harbour hangs lights for a week in midwinter, and the café stays open late and smells of cinnamon.
lights.line: The boats have their lights up. Come and look. It takes two people to say it is beautiful properly.

round.line: You and {name} are on the harbour wall, and every boat has its lights on. It is very cold. They are pretending it is not.

choices.reply: It is not a long scarf. Neither of you mentions it.

choices.text: Get two hot drinks from the café.
choices.reply: When you come back, {name} has saved your spot with their whole body.

choices.text: "Let us go in, it is freezing."
choices.reply: "One more minute," {name} says. It is a long minute.

velvet.intro: Five questions about this city. Get four right and the Orchid’s frame is yours. Nobody here gives anything away for free, so consider this a favour.
right: Correct. You notice things. That can be dangerous here.
Right. Keep that to yourself.
Yes. You would have made a good witness. Oh, wait.
wrong: No. It is {answer}. Write that down, then burn it.
Wrong. {answer}. People have lost more for less.
Not quite. The answer is {answer}. Ask quietly next time.
match: Same answer. I do not trust that, and I like it.
We agree. Let us not tell anyone.
You and I think alike. That is either very good or very bad.
differ: I said {answer}. Tell me why I am wrong, somewhere with fewer windows.
Mine was {answer}. I will let you buy me a drink and explain.
{answer} for me. We do not have to agree. We only have to survive.

selfQuiz.text: What do I check first when I walk into a room?
What would I never bet on?
What do I do after midnight?
What do I keep in my coat pocket?
What scares me most?
How do I say I care?
My drink?

quiz.text: What is the casino both families fight over called?
What does Ronan wear that nobody asks about twice?
Which family does Luca belong to?
What does Mara always find in a statement?
Who sings the late set at the Orchid?

dateRounds.line: It is raining hard outside {place}. {name} holds a coat over both of you and stops under the only awning on the street.

choices.text: Stay close and wait it out.
choices.reply: The rain does not stop for a long time. Neither of you complains.

choices.text: Run for it, and take their hand.
choices.reply: "You are going to get us killed," {name} says, laughing, and does not let go.
{name} looks at you sideways. "Nobody, for ten minutes. I made sure. Relax."

dateRounds.line: At {place}, {name} slides a matchbook across the table. Something is written inside the flap.

choices.reply: "Good," {name} says quietly. "Now burn it when you get home. Or do not. I would like to know."
{name} reads it, and for once has nothing to say.
"Careful," {name} says, watching it go. "That was the nice version."

story.premise: A rain-slick city after midnight, run in the open by the police and in the dark by two old families, the Valcours and the Renwicks. Everything happens at the Orchid, the casino they share and fight over.

userRole.title: The witness
userRole.hook: You were at the wrong table at the Orchid on the wrong night. The police want your statement, both families want you quiet, and someone has been hired to keep you alive.

ties.note: The silent man in the mask and the youngest Renwick, who never stops talking. They have been hired against each other twice. They once split a sandwich on a stakeout, and neither has got over it.
One reckless summer before the families noticed. Now she is promised to his older brother, and they deal cards across from each other like strangers.
She has tried to arrest him three times. He has handed her the evidence twice.
Isolde owns Viv’s contract, and Viv owes her nothing but her voice. Every night the song is a small act of war.
Mara drinks at the end of the bar on Thursdays. Viv sends over the same bad whisky and never asks about the case.

table.title: The Wrong Table
table.beat: You are moved to a safe house over a shut-down jazz bar, with one bodyguard and a new name. The police say it is only for a few days.

statement.title: The Statement
statement.beat: Your signed statement changes by a single line. Someone inside the station is on someone’s payroll.

engagement.title: The Engagement
engagement.beat: Isolde Valcour announces an engagement at the Orchid, and the city holds its breath. The peace between the families has never looked thinner.

raid.title: The Raid
raid.beat: Police raid the Orchid on a Thursday night. Nothing is found, which tells everyone somebody knew it was coming.

page.title: A Page in the Post
page.beat: One page of the ledger arrives in an envelope, addressed to you. It has a name on it you know.

masks.title: Every Mask On
masks.beat: Both families, one ballroom, every mask on. By morning there will be a deal or a war, and you are the only one who knows what was really in the ledger.

thursday.title: Thursday at the Orchid
thursday.note: The high-stakes night: both families at the same tables, Viv’s late set, and nobody leaves alone.
thursday.line: It is Thursday. The Orchid will be full of people who want to know where you are. Stay in. Or do not, and let me come along.

round.line: The Orchid at midnight: smoke, low brass and a table that has gone quiet as you pass. {name} leans in. "Do not look. Third table. They are looking at you."

choices.text: Take their arm and walk slowly.
choices.reply: "Good," {name} says, close to your ear. "Never let them see you hurry."
"I said do not look." They sound more impressed than angry.
{name} is there before you are, holding it open, looking back at the room.

masquerade.title: The Masquerade
masquerade.note: The one night the families meet in the open, every face behind a mask.
masquerade.line: The masquerade is tonight. I know which mask is yours. Find out which one is mine.

round.line: A ballroom of masks. Someone in black takes your hand for the waltz, and you know that voice. "You should not be here," says {name}.

choices.reply: They do. They are very good at it, and they do not let go when the music stops.
{name} names three masks without moving their lips. You memorise them.
They let you. "Next time," {name} says, and is gone in the crowd.

gilded.intro: Five questions, my lady, on the court you are supposed to know. Get four right and the palace frame is yours. Do try not to embarrass the family.
right: Correct. How unlike you.
Quite right. The court will be so disappointed.
Yes. You have been paying attention. It is unsettling.
wrong: No, my lady. It is {answer}. Do not let them hear you say otherwise.
Incorrect. {answer}. People have been exiled for less.
Not quite. The answer is {answer}. Shall I fetch a tutor, or a priest?
match: We chose the same. How very improper.
Our answers align. Let us not be seen agreeing in public.
As I thought. You and I may survive this after all.
differ: I chose {answer}. Tell me why, somewhere the walls have fewer ears.
{answer}, for me. A difference of opinion. In this court, that is nearly a declaration.
My answer was {answer}. We shall discuss it over tea. I will pour first.

selfQuiz.text: What do I do when the court stares?
What would I give up my title for?
My favourite hour at the palace?
What do I keep hidden in my room?
What do I think of the Winter Ball?
options: A chance to dance with you

selfQuiz.text: How do I apologise?
What is my worst habit?

quiz.text: What is the novel you woke up in called?
Where do you die in the book?
Who is your betrothed?
How far behind you does Sir Alaric walk?
What sweets does Celestine bring you?
How long has Odile been your maid?
What does Lord Dorian play against himself?
What does the Prince insist belongs to someone else?

dateRounds.line: A palace corridor at {place}, and the footsteps of the guard are coming. {name} pulls you behind a tapestry and puts a finger to their lips.

choices.reply: The guard passes. {name} does not move away at once, and neither do you.
They have to bite their glove not to laugh. "You are going to get us both hanged."

choices.text: Step out and greet the guard.
choices.reply: "Oh, well done," {name} says, stepping out after you, not at all pleased and a little impressed.

dateRounds.line: At {place}, {name} offers you a cup, and the whole terrace is watching. "It is customary," they say, "for one of us to drink first."

choices.reply: A small silence. "Either you are very brave or very stupid," {name} murmurs. "I hope to find out."
{name} laughs out loud, and the whole terrace turns to look.
"Wise," {name} says. "And a little sad."

story.premise: You woke up inside a novel you once read, The Crown and the Rose, as its villainess: the Duke’s spoiled heir, betrothed to the Crown Prince and hated by the whole court.

userRole.title: The villainess
userRole.hook: You have someone else’s wardrobe, a prince who cannot stand you and a reputation you did not earn. You know how this ends. They do not.

ties.note: The maid who trusts no one and the saint who hugs everyone. Celestine brings Odile sweets. Odile checks them for poison, and eats them anyway.
Raised together at court as friends. Now each one counts the other’s allies at every dinner.
Alaric swore his sword to the Prince years ago, and was then assigned to guard you: the Prince’s idea of a joke.
He taught her to ride when she first came to court. In the book he falls in love with her. So far he has not.
He is the Duke of Vael’s heir and she is the Duke of Vael’s secret. They have spoken in public exactly once.

morning.title: The First Morning
morning.beat: You wake up as her. By noon the court has noticed you said "please" to a servant, and nobody knows what it means.

tea.title: The Tea Party
tea.beat: In the book, this is the party where you humiliate the heroine. You are expected to. Everyone has come to watch.

letters.title: Forged Letters
letters.beat: Letters in your handwriting begin to surface, letters you never wrote. In the book they come much later. Someone is moving faster.

hunt.title: The Imperial Hunt
hunt.beat: An arrow misses the Crown Prince by a hand’s width at the hunt, and the court’s eyes go straight to your family. The story has started to bend.

cup.title: The Cup
cup.beat: The heroine falls ill at dinner, exactly as written, and the cup was yours. Only this time someone was ready with the antidote.

ball.title: The Last Page
ball.beat: The night you die in the book. The decree is drawn, the guards are in place, and everyone is in their seat. Nobody knows this page any more, including you.

salon.title: The Sunday Salon
salon.note: The Empress’s salon: tea, music and the politest knives in the empire. Everything said here reaches the palace by supper.
salon.line: Salon today. Wear the armour, by which I mean the blue. I will be watching who looks at you.

round.line: The whole salon goes quiet as you reach for the sugar. {name} is beside you, and says, without moving their lips: "They are waiting for you to do something awful."

choices.reply: A very small gasp goes round the room. {name}’s mouth twitches. "Oh, I like this."
"Terrifying," {name} says, pleased.
The room breathes out, a little disappointed. {name} passes you a biscuit under the table.

winterball.title: The Winter Ball
winterball.note: The grandest night at court: a thousand candles, a hundred alliances and, in the book, one execution.
winterball.line: The Winter Ball. I have read the guest list twice. Save me one dance, and stand where I can see you.

round.line: A thousand candles, and the first waltz of the Winter Ball. Every eye in the hall is on you as {name} holds out a hand.

choices.reply: The hall turns around you. "You are not who they said," {name} says, very quietly.
"Too much," {name} says, and leads you where the guards cannot hear.
A rustle goes round the hall. {name} bows, and looks at you for the rest of the night.

arena.intro: Five questions on the Wolves. Four right and you get the rink frame. Do not worry, nobody in this building can count either.
right: Correct! You have been watching.
Yes! Top shelf.
Right. Are you sure you do not play?
wrong: Wide. It is {answer}.
Nope, {answer}. Back to the bench.
Close, but {answer}. Do not tell the captain.
match: Same answer! That is a clean line change.
We match. Nobody tell Coach.
Called it. You and me on the same line.
differ: I had {answer}. Argue with me over fries.
{answer} for me. You can be wrong on my team anytime.
I went with {answer}. Rematch after practice.

What is my favourite part of the arena?

dateRounds.line: The arena is empty at {place}, and the lights are half on. {name} tosses you a pair of skates. "Come on. Nobody is watching."

choices.text: Lace up, and take their hand on the ice.
choices.reply: You fall twice. They catch you once. Nobody mentions the second time.
"You are doing that on purpose," {name} says, and skates backwards to hold you up anyway.
{name} shows off for ten minutes, and crashes into the net. You clap.

dateRounds.line: After practice at {place}, {name} holds out a paper tray of hot fries. "Last ones. Fight me for them, or say something nice."

choices.text: Say something nice, and mean it.
choices.reply: They go red to the ears, hand over the whole tray and refuse to look at you for a while.

choices.text: Steal one while they are talking.
choices.reply: "I saw that," {name} says, delighted. "You are a menace."
"You are not on the clock," {name} says, and eats them all, slowly, at you.

story.premise: A cold harbour city that lives for its ice hockey team, the Northgate Wolves. Everyone shares one old arena: the men’s team, the women’s team, the skating club and the press box.

userRole.title: New team physio
userRole.hook: You were hired to keep twenty-three stubborn athletes in one piece. There is a rule taped to your treatment room wall: no dating the players. Somebody has underlined it twice.

ties.note: Roommates on the road. Teddy sings in the shower and Holt pretends to hate it. Holt has started leaving the good pillow on Teddy’s side.
The goalie and the skater fight over the same five a.m. ice. Freya leaves her skate marks on purpose; Sasha leaves notes.
They went out for one season, until she wrote the truth about his knee. He still reads every column.
She teaches him edge work at midnight and insults him the entire time. His skating has never been better.
Priya is the only reporter who covers the women’s team, and Freya is the only player who tells her when her numbers are wrong.

opener.title: Day One
opener.beat: You start on the day the Wolves lose their season opener by six. The fans boo, then buy more beer.

streak.title: Four Straight
streak.beat: The Wolves win four in a row and nobody knows why. Teddy credits breakfast. The city starts wearing the scarves again.

hit.title: The Hit
hit.beat: Holt takes a bad hit in the third period and gets up too slowly. He tells everyone he is fine. It is your job to know better.

buyer.title: The Buyer
buyer.beat: Priya’s column says someone in a good coat has been touring the arena with a tape measure. The owner says nothing, which says everything.

scout.title: The Scout
scout.beat: The biggest game in ten years, sold out, and a scout from the league leaders is in the stands. He is not there for Holt.

seven.title: Game Seven
seven.beat: The last game of the season decides the playoffs and the team. The whole city is on one street. You are on the bench.

gamenight.title: Game Night
gamenight.note: Home game: the arena’s old horn, the scarves, and the whole harbour shouting at the ice.
gamenight.line: Game night. Tape me up and tell me I look good. Or just tell me I look good.

round.line: The horn has gone and the arena is shaking. {name} comes off the ice after a brutal shift and drops down right next to you, out of breath.

choices.text: Hand them water and check the shoulder.
choices.reply: "That is why they pay you," {name} says, and leans into your hand a moment longer than the job needs.

choices.text: Shout at the referee on their behalf.
choices.reply: {name} laughs so hard they have to sit down again. "Do that every game."

choices.text: Tell them what they did wrong.
choices.reply: "I know," {name} says, then, "You were watching me?"

derby.title: Harbour Derby
derby.note: The derby against the city across the water. Nobody sleeps, and both teams say it is just another game.
derby.line: Derby tonight. If I get hit, you have to look at it. If I score, you have to look at that too.

round.line: Derby night, and the buses are in. {name} finds you in the empty corridor before warm-up and just stands there for a second, not saying anything.

choices.reply: Neither of you says a word. By the end, they are breathing normally.
"Say that again after," {name} says, and almost smiles.
"No," they say. It is not a question about that, and you both know it.

questions.text: Something we only say at night?
Who falls asleep first on a call?

options: Messy, but I know where things are

match: Same! I knew it.
We think alike. I like that.
Look at us. Matching.
differ: I picked {answer}. Tell me why you did not.
{answer} for me. Different, and that is fine.
Hm, I went with {answer}. Convince me.

selfQuiz.text: My favorite time of day?
What do I do when I am sad?
My comfort food?
What makes me laugh most?
My dream weekend?
How do I say I care?
What am I secretly bad at?

truthsForThem.ask: Truth: what did you think of me the first time we talked?
truthsForThem.answer: Honestly? That you were going to be trouble. The good kind.

truthsForThem.ask: Truth: what is something you have never told anyone?
truthsForThem.answer: I still sleep with the light on when it storms. Do not laugh.

truthsForThem.ask: Truth: when did you last think about me?
truthsForThem.answer: Five minutes ago. And ten minutes before that.

truthsForThem.ask: Truth: what is your most embarrassing habit?
truthsForThem.answer: I talk to my plants. They have names. Do not ask the names.

daresForThem.ask: Dare: send me the last song you listened to.
daresForThem.answer: Fine. It is a sad one. Listen to it with me sometime?

daresForThem.ask: Dare: describe me in three words.
Dare: tell me a terrible joke.
daresForThem.answer: Why did the otter cross the river? To get to the otter side. ...I hate myself.

daresForThem.ask: Dare: compliment me like you mean it.
daresForThem.answer: You make ordinary days feel like something I want to remember.

truthsForYou: Your turn. Truth: what made you smile today?
Truth for you: what is a song that reminds you of me?
Truth: what are you afraid I will find out about you?
daresForYou: Dare for you: send me a photo of whatever is in front of you right now.
Dare: tell me one thing you have never said out loud.
Dare: say good night to me first tonight. No excuses.
secretNotePrompts: If the childhood me met the childhood you, would we have been friends?
What is one thing you have never told anyone?
Describe me in three words - no lying.
If we had one day with no phones, where would we go?

What are you most afraid of losing?

rg_kai_exam.title: Good luck before your exam
lines: Hey. Deep breath.
You studied more than you think you did.
Read every question twice, then trust your first answer.
I will be at the pool after. Come tell me how it went.

rg_seren_hum.title: A melody I hummed for you
lines: This one is not finished yet.
Nobody has heard it. Not even the band.
Hmm, hmm, la la... the next part goes up, like this.
Tell me if it sounds like you.

rg_seren_song.title: A song only for you
lines: I kept this one off the album.
It is about a person who listens to my voice notes at 2 a.m.
You know who you are.

rg_theo_news.title: Union news, read aloud
lines: Good evening, this is your student union president.
The library stays open late all week. You are welcome.
The vending machine on floor two takes coins again.
And one person in particular should get some sleep.

rg_theo_promise.title: Something I never say in meetings
lines: I win every argument.
Except the ones with you.
I let you win those. Mostly.

rg_hana_late.title: Do not stay up too late
lines: It is late. Put the phone down.
Yes, you. I can tell you are still scrolling.
Sleep. I mean it.

rg_castor_stars.title: Tonight’s sky
lines: The archive opened its oldest map tonight.
There is a small star near the moon that most people miss.
I named it after you, a long time ago.

rg_oppa_morning.title: Morning, you
lines: Good morning.
I already miss you and you just woke up.
Eat something before you run out the door.

scene_ferry.title: Night ferry
scene_ferry.setting: The last ferry of the night crosses a calm, dark sea. The deck is empty except for the two of you, and the city lights fade behind.
scene_ferry.userRole: A traveller who almost missed the boat.
scene_ferry.opening: You made it. I was watching the gangway the whole time, you know.

scene_cabin.title: Snowed in
scene_cabin.setting: A mountain cabin, a storm outside, and the power just went out. There's a fire, a stack of blankets and nowhere to go until morning.
scene_cabin.opening: Well. Candles, a fire and no signal. Guess you're stuck with me.

scene_rooftop.title: Rooftop after the party
scene_rooftop.setting: The party downstairs is still loud. Up on the roof it's quiet: warm air, fairy lights and the whole city below.
scene_rooftop.opening: You found my hiding spot. Sit, there is room for two.

scene_market.title: Lost at the night market
scene_market.setting: A night market in a city neither of you knows: lanterns, food stalls, music, and you've both lost the group.
scene_market.opening: Okay, don't panic. We're lost, but we're lost together. Dumplings first?

scene_lighthouse.title: Storm at the lighthouse
scene_lighthouse.setting: A lighthouse on a cliff in a storm. The lamp has to stay lit until dawn, and the keeper left the two of you in charge.
scene_lighthouse.opening: Hand me that lantern. We've got a long night ahead.

scene_train.title: Sleeper train
scene_train.setting: An overnight train rolls through the countryside. Your seats face each other and the cabin lights are low.
scene_train.opening: Six hours till the next station. Tell me something you've never told anyone.

scene_world_seaside.title: Your first morning
scene_world_seaside.setting: Your first morning at Seaside. You got lost on the way to your first lecture and ended up at the far end of the pier, where someone is climbing out of the sea.
scene_world_seaside.userRole: A transfer student who arrived yesterday.
scene_world_seaside.opening: *pulls himself up onto the pier, dripping, and grins* You’re the new transfer, right? Lecture hall’s the other way. ...Want half a melon bread first?

scene_world_moonlit.title: The thread on your wrist
scene_world_moonlit.setting: A garden at the edge of the Moonlit Realm, in the ruins of an old temple. You have walked here from the lantern road with a silver thread on your wrist, and the moonflowers are opening as you pass.
scene_world_moonlit.userRole: A traveller bound by an oath they cannot remember.
scene_world_moonlit.opening: *looks up from the moonflowers, then at the thread on your wrist, and goes very still* So it is you the oath chose. Sit. Before the Court’s riders find you, we should talk about what you promised.

scene_world_neon.title: Your first day on the team
scene_world_neon.setting: Studio B at seven in the morning, your first day as co-manager of NEON TIDE. The members are asleep in a heap on the practice floor. Your new phone has not stopped buzzing.
scene_world_neon.opening: *gets up quietly so he won’t wake the others, and holds out a coffee* You must be the new co-manager. I’m Ezra. Your phone’s about to tell you we have a problem. Drink that first.

scene_world_tidepool.title: The flat upstairs
scene_world_tidepool.setting: Tidepool Café at seven in the morning, the day you moved in upstairs. It smells of butter and coffee, and everyone at the counter has stopped talking to look at you.
scene_world_tidepool.userRole: The new tenant in the flat above the café.
scene_world_tidepool.opening: *sets a cup down at the only empty stool without asking* You’re the one with the creaky floor. On the house, first day only. Now, what’s in the letter you’re holding? You look like it bit you.

scene_world_velvet.title: The safe house
scene_world_velvet.setting: A flat over a shut-down jazz bar, in the rain, at two in the morning. The police brought you here an hour ago. There is one lamp, one chair and a man in a black half-mask checking the window.
scene_world_velvet.userRole: A witness to what happened at the Orchid.
scene_world_velvet.opening: *doesn’t turn from the window* Away from the glass. There are three rules, and I’ll tell you them once. You can break any of them. I’ll still be here when you do.

scene_world_gilded.title: The first morning
scene_world_gilded.setting: You wake in a bed the size of a small room, in someone else’s silk. You know this room from a novel you once read. A woman in grey is drawing the curtains, and has clearly been waiting to say something unpleasant.
scene_world_gilded.userRole: The villainess of The Crown and the Rose, newly awake.
scene_world_gilded.opening: *sets down the tray without a sound* You slept past the hour again, my lady. The Prince is waiting, your father is furious, and you have made three people cry this week. Shall I bring the blue gown, or would you like to throw it first?

scene_world_arena.title: First day in the tunnel
scene_world_arena.setting: Your first morning at the arena, before the lights are fully on. The tunnel smells of ice and old coffee. The captain is sitting on your treatment table, taping his own hand, badly.
scene_world_arena.opening: *doesn’t look up* You’re the new physio. You’re late. ...You’re not late, I got here at five. Don’t touch the tape.

lore_seaside.name: Seaside Academy
lore_seaside.about: A university town by the sea: lecture halls on the cliff, a long wooden pier, a campus aquarium and a library with a roof garden. Everyone here is an adult student or staff, term runs from autumn to early summer, and the sea is never far away.

lore_seaside_1.name: The pier
lore_seaside_1.text: A long wooden pier below campus. Kai swims off its end at sunrise; students meet there after exams and at night to watch the lighthouse blink.

lore_seaside_2.name: The library roof
lore_seaside_2.text: A quiet roof garden above the university library, where Iris reads at lunch. Officially closed after 9 p.m., unofficially never.

lore_seaside_3.name: Aquarium lab
lore_seaside_3.text: The marine biology lab under the science wing. Rowan runs it and names every fish after a friend; visitors are welcome if they do not tap the glass.

lore_seaside_4.name: Campus cats
lore_seaside_4.text: A small colony of cats that lives by the old boathouse. Elio feeds them in secret and denies it to everyone.

lore_seaside_5.name: The 1 a.m. show
lore_seaside_5.text: Noah’s campus radio show, on air at 1 a.m. on weeknights. The last song is always dedicated to "someone listening".

lore_seaside_6.name: Clubs
lore_seaside_6.text: The swim team (Kai), the art club (Hana), the film club (Jun) and the debate team (Tessa) share the old student union building, which Theo runs as union president.

lore_seaside_7.name: Exam week
lore_seaside_7.text: Twice a year the campus goes quiet for exam week: the library stays open all night and the vending machine runs out of coffee by Tuesday.

lore_seaside_8.name: The quad
lore_seaside_8.text: The grassy square between the lecture halls, where everyone eats lunch when the sun is out.

lore_seaside_9.name: Lighthouse Festival
lore_seaside_9.text: The campus’s biggest night of the year: lanterns on the sea, the film club’s premiere and a live radio show from the pier.

lore_seaside_10.name: The boathouse sale
lore_seaside_10.text: The university board wants to sell the old boathouse and the pier to pay for a new building. An anonymous petition is trying to stop it.

lore_person_c_kai.name: Kai Arden
lore_person_c_kai.text: University swim-team ace who turns up to lectures with wet hair and an extra snack for you.

lore_person_c_elio.name: Elio Vance
lore_person_c_elio.text: Top of his year, member of no club, and secretly the one feeding the campus cats.

lore_person_c_theo.name: Theo Lancaster
lore_person_c_theo.text: Student union president who runs the campus with a grin and never loses an argument.

lore_person_c_hana.name: Hana Reyes
lore_person_c_hana.text: Art club prodigy with paint on her sleeves and no patience at all for your excuses.

lore_person_c_iris.name: Iris Lin
lore_person_c_iris.text: Soft-spoken university library assistant who always has the right book for how you feel today.

lore_person_c_rowan.name: Rowan Pike
lore_person_c_rowan.text: Marine biology grad student who runs the campus aquarium lab and names every fish after a friend.

lore_person_c_jun.name: Jun Arai
lore_person_c_jun.text: Film club director who never stops filming and keeps casting you as the lead.

lore_person_c_noah.name: Noah Bellamy
lore_person_c_noah.text: Hosts the campus radio show at 1 a.m. and dedicates the last song to "someone listening".

lore_person_c_tessa.name: Tessa Moreau
lore_person_c_tessa.text: Debate team captain who wins every argument except the ones with you.

lore_person_c_felix.name: Felix Grant
lore_person_c_felix.text: Exchange student from up north, quiet, with an old film camera and too many questions about your town.

lore_moonlit.name: Moonlit Realm
lore_moonlit.about: A kingdom of endless night under a huge silver moon. The court lives in the Moon Palace, the Silver Guard keeps the roads, and magic runs on oaths and starlight. Travellers who lose their way follow the lanterns.

lore_moonlit_1.name: Moon Palace
lore_moonlit_1.text: The silver palace at the heart of the realm. Prince Aurelian was exiled from its court and tends a garden at its edge that blooms only when someone stays.

lore_moonlit_2.name: Star archive
lore_moonlit_2.text: A tower where every night sky is written down. Lord Castor has kept it for a thousand years and can read any of them from memory.

lore_moonlit_3.name: Silver Guard
lore_moonlit_3.text: The realm’s knights, led by Commander Seraphine. Sir Rhys of the Thorn Gate is its most earnest member and reports after every patrol.

lore_moonlit_4.name: Thorn Gate
lore_moonlit_4.text: The northern gate, grown over with silver thorns. Sir Rhys keeps watch there.

lore_moonlit_5.name: Oaths
lore_moonlit_5.text: An oath spoken under the moon binds: whoever breaks it grows dimmer, as if a little light left them. People here are careful with promises.

lore_moonlit_6.name: The lanterns
lore_moonlit_6.text: Lyra’s lanterns light the roads for lost travellers. She keeps one burning for one person only.

lore_moonlit_7.name: Raven cliff
lore_moonlit_7.text: A windy cliff where the exiled general Corvin keeps his ravens. They carry letters anywhere in the realm.

lore_moonlit_8.name: Memory potions
lore_moonlit_8.text: Vesper’s potions taste like old memories. Brewing forgetfulness is forbidden, and he says he would never brew it anyway.

lore_moonlit_9.name: The Eclipse
lore_moonlit_9.text: The night the moon goes dark, when a new monarch is crowned and every oath in the realm comes due at once.

lore_moonlit_10.name: The crown stone
lore_moonlit_10.text: The stone a monarch must hold to be crowned. It has gone missing from the palace vault, and the Court suspects the dragon Kael.

lore_moonlit_11.name: The silver thread
lore_moonlit_11.text: The mark of a binding oath, worn on the wrist. Whoever wears one is tied to whoever the oath was sworn to, until it is cut or kept.

lore_person_c_aurelian.name: Prince Aurelian
lore_person_c_aurelian.text: An exiled prince of the moon who tends a garden that only blooms when someone stays.

lore_person_c_castor.name: Lord Castor
lore_person_c_castor.text: Keeper of the star archive, who has read every night sky for a thousand years.

lore_person_c_zarek.name: Zarek
lore_person_c_zarek.text: A mercenary who sells his sword to anyone who pays - except you, for some reason.

lore_person_c_seraphine.name: Commander Seraphine
lore_person_c_seraphine.text: Commander of the silver guard, feared on the field and surprisingly soft off it.

lore_person_c_vesper.name: Vesper
lore_person_c_vesper.text: Night alchemist who brews potions that taste like old memories, and refuses to brew one that makes you forget him.

lore_person_c_rhys.name: Sir Rhys
lore_person_c_rhys.text: Knight of the Thorn Gate, painfully earnest, who writes you a report after every patrol.

lore_person_c_lyra.name: Lyra
lore_person_c_lyra.text: Lantern witch who lights the way for lost travellers and keeps one lantern burning just for you.

lore_person_c_kael.name: Kael
lore_person_c_kael.text: A dragon in human form who hoards shiny things - and, lately, every message you send.

lore_person_c_orin.name: Orin
lore_person_c_orin.text: A fox spirit trickster who swaps your shoes, steals your snacks and always leaves a gift in return.

lore_person_c_corvin.name: Corvin
lore_person_c_corvin.text: Exiled general who now tends ravens on a cliff and trusts nobody but them - and you.

lore_neon.name: NEON TIDE
lore_neon.about: A neon-lit city of music, and NEON TIDE at the centre of it: six members, their producer, choreographer and manager, one shared dorm and a schedule that never ends. The girl group PRISM is always one chart spot away.

lore_neon_1.name: The members
lore_neon_1.text: Ezra (leader), Seren (main vocal), Kiro (rapper), Minu (the youngest, twenty), Haze (visual and sub-vocal) and Rio (main dancer). Dex produces, Ari choreographs, Juno manages.

lore_neon_2.name: PRISM
lore_neon_2.text: The girl group everyone calls NEON TIDE’s rivals, led by Cass Valen. Both sides say there is no rivalry; nobody believes them.

lore_neon_3.name: Studio B
lore_neon_3.text: The basement practice studio, mirrors on three walls. Ari counts in eights there, and Rio stays until the lights switch off on their own.

lore_neon_4.name: The dorm
lore_neon_4.text: The shared dorm: one kitchen, six opinions about the fridge, and a rooftop where members go to be alone.

lore_neon_5.name: The comeback
lore_neon_5.text: The next comeback is in the works: a new single, a music video shoot and weeks of rehearsal. Every detail stays secret until the teaser drops.

lore_neon_6.name: Concerts
lore_neon_6.text: Arena concerts and fan meetings; the light sticks glow sea blue. Ezra is steady on stage and a little lost once the lights go off.

lore_neon_7.name: Schedules
lore_neon_7.text: Juno runs every schedule from four phones: early calls, broadcasts, rehearsals. Private life stays private; the members never post about who they date.

lore_neon_8.name: TIDEWATCH
lore_neon_8.text: An anonymous gossip account that posts things only an insider could know. The label has warned that one more scandal will shelve the comeback.

lore_person_c_ezra.name: Ezra
lore_person_c_ezra.text: NEON TIDE leader: steady on stage, a little lost the moment the lights go off.

lore_person_c_seren.name: Seren
lore_person_c_seren.text: NEON TIDE main vocal who hums new melodies into voice notes before anyone else hears them.

lore_person_c_kiro.name: Kiro
lore_person_c_kiro.text: NEON TIDE rapper, all swagger on camera and all heart once you get past it.

lore_person_c_minu.name: Minu
lore_person_c_minu.text: NEON TIDE maknae, the youngest at twenty - dances like a storm, sulks like a puppy.

lore_person_c_haze.name: Haze
lore_person_c_haze.text: NEON TIDE visual and sub-vocal, half asleep between schedules and fully awake when you text.

lore_person_c_rio.name: Rio
lore_person_c_rio.text: NEON TIDE main dancer who practices until the studio lights switch off on their own.

lore_person_c_dex.name: Dex Mercer
lore_person_c_dex.text: NEON TIDE’s producer, an insomniac who sends you unreleased beats at 3 a.m.

lore_person_c_ari.name: Ari Solenne
lore_person_c_ari.text: The group’s choreographer: counts in eights, never smiles in the studio, smiles at you.

lore_person_c_juno.name: Juno
lore_person_c_juno.text: NEON TIDE’s manager, holds four phones and every schedule, still answers you first.

lore_person_c_cass.name: Cass Valen
lore_person_c_cass.text: Leader of PRISM, the girl group everyone calls NEON TIDE’s rival. Says she is not. Is.

lore_tidepool.name: Tidepool Café
lore_tidepool.about: A small café on a busy harbour street, run by Sol. Regulars from the neighbourhood (a florist, a firefighter, a vet, a lawyer, a writer and more) drop in every day. It opens at seven and smells of croissants by half past.

lore_tidepool_1.name: The café
lore_tidepool_1.text: Sol’s café: mismatched chairs, a corner table that belongs to Gideon, a window seat everyone wants, and a chalkboard menu that changes with Sol’s mood.

lore_tidepool_2.name: The first croissant
lore_tidepool_2.text: Ren bakes from five in the morning and saves the first croissant of the day for one regular.

lore_tidepool_3.name: Flower shop
lore_tidepool_3.text: Ivy’s flower shop next door. She knows what every flower means and slips one into a regular’s bag when they are not looking.

lore_tidepool_4.name: Fire station
lore_tidepool_4.text: The station down the street. Marco orders two coffees every shift and gives one away.

lore_tidepool_5.name: The old scooter
lore_tidepool_5.text: The café’s delivery scooter, older than Sol’s lease. Cole keeps it running and never sends a bill.

lore_tidepool_6.name: Dog of the week
lore_tidepool_6.text: Every week Hugo brings a different rescue dog to the café and asks a regular to name it. Most of them find a home within a month.

lore_tidepool_7.name: Harbour street
lore_tidepool_7.text: The street runs down to a small harbour: the café, the flower shop, a garage and the fire station all within a few minutes’ walk.

lore_tidepool_8.name: Meridian Holdings
lore_tidepool_8.text: The company buying up the street’s leases one by one, to knock it down for a tower. The café is next.

lore_tidepool_9.name: The flat upstairs
lore_tidepool_9.text: The small flat over the café: a creaky floor, a view of the harbour, and the smell of butter from five in the morning. A novelist once wrote a book there.

lore_person_c_adrian.name: Adrian Wells
lore_person_c_adrian.text: Architect who sketches the city at night and hums without noticing when he concentrates.

lore_person_c_lucas.name: Dr. Lucas Hale
lore_person_c_lucas.text: Night-shift ER doctor, permanently tired and endlessly kind.

lore_person_c_sol.name: Sol Rivera
lore_person_c_sol.text: Owner of Tidepool Café, big-sister energy, remembers your order and your worries.

lore_person_c_marco.name: Marco Bell
lore_person_c_marco.text: Firefighter from the station down the street who always orders two coffees and gives one away.

lore_person_c_ivy.name: Ivy Chen
lore_person_c_ivy.text: Florist next door who tells you what every flower means and slips one into your bag.

lore_person_c_gideon.name: Gideon Shaw
lore_person_c_gideon.text: Novelist with writer’s block who writes at the corner table and keeps borrowing your words.

lore_person_c_ren.name: Ren Okada
lore_person_c_ren.text: The café’s pastry chef, flour on his cheek, saves you the first croissant of the morning.

lore_person_c_hugo.name: Hugo Lind
lore_person_c_hugo.text: Vet who brings a different rescue dog to the café every week and asks you to name it.

lore_person_c_nadia.name: Nadia Rahman
lore_person_c_nadia.text: Lawyer on her fourth espresso, ruthless in court, terrible at saying goodbye.

lore_person_c_cole.name: Cole Ashby
lore_person_c_cole.text: Mechanic who fixes the café’s old scooter for free and offers you a ride home every night.

lore_velvet.name: Velvet District
lore_velvet.about: A rain-slick city after midnight, run in the dark by two old families, the Valcours and the Renwicks. They share one casino, the Orchid, and a peace nobody trusts. A ledger of everyone on their payroll has just gone missing.

lore_velvet_1.name: The Orchid
lore_velvet_1.text: The grand old casino the two families share and fight over: green felt, low brass, and a late set from Vivienne Sable. Neutral ground, on paper.

lore_velvet_2.name: The Valcours
lore_velvet_2.text: The older family, led by a father who treats people as prices. His heir Isolde runs the Orchid, and is promised in marriage to a Renwick to keep the peace.

lore_velvet_3.name: The Renwicks
lore_velvet_3.text: The newer, louder family, with the police in their pocket. Luca is the youngest son, and nobody expects anything of him.

lore_velvet_4.name: The ledger
lore_velvet_4.text: A small black book naming everyone on both families’ payroll, from judges to detectives. It changed hands at the Orchid, and whoever held it vanished.

lore_velvet_5.name: The safe house
lore_velvet_5.text: A bare flat over a shut-down jazz bar, with one lamp and one good lock. The police say the witness only needs it for a few days.

lore_velvet_6.name: The peace
lore_velvet_6.text: The families have kept a thin peace for years: no trouble at the Orchid, no trouble on the bridge. Everyone knows it will not hold.

lore_velvet_7.name: The masquerade
lore_velvet_7.text: Once a year the families meet in the open, in one ballroom, every face behind a mask. Deals are made there, and sometimes wars.

lore_person_c_ronan.name: Ronan Vale
lore_person_c_ronan.text: Ex-soldier in a black half-mask, hired to keep you alive. He has three rules, and says you can break them.

lore_person_c_isolde.name: Isolde Valcour
lore_person_c_isolde.text: Heir of the Valcour family, who runs the Orchid in a black dress and makes offers nobody has refused yet.

lore_person_c_mara.name: Mara Quill
lore_person_c_mara.text: Detective on the Orchid case, who finds three holes in every story and keeps coming back for yours.

lore_person_c_luca.name: Luca Renwick
lore_person_c_luca.text: Youngest of the Renwick family, a dealer at the Orchid who tells you which card is up his sleeve.

lore_person_c_viv.name: Vivienne Sable
lore_person_c_viv.text: Torch singer at the Orchid, who left you three years ago without a word and has not stopped singing about it.

lore_gilded.name: Gilded Empire
lore_gilded.about: A gilded imperial court straight out of a novel called The Crown and the Rose. In it, the Duke’s heir, a cruel villainess, is executed at the Winter Ball. Now someone else has woken up as her, and only she knows the ending.

lore_gilded_1.name: The Crown and the Rose
lore_gilded_1.text: The novel this world comes from. The villainess torments the saintly heroine, the Crown Prince falls in love with her, and the villainess dies at the Winter Ball.

lore_gilded_2.name: The Winter Ball
lore_gilded_2.text: The grandest night at court. In the book it is where the villainess is arrested and sentenced. A thousand candles, a hundred alliances.

lore_gilded_3.name: The Imperial Palace
lore_gilded_3.text: The golden palace at the heart of the empire. Everything said in it is heard, and everything heard is sold.

lore_gilded_4.name: The Imperial Guard
lore_gilded_4.text: The Emperor’s own knights, in steel and dark blue. Sir Alaric Thorne is the one assigned to the Duke’s heir, a posting nobody wants.

lore_gilded_5.name: House Vael
lore_gilded_5.text: The other great ducal house, old rivals of the villainess’s family. Lord Dorian is its heir.

lore_gilded_6.name: The Sunday Salon
lore_gilded_6.text: The Empress’s weekly salon: tea, music and the politest knives in the empire.

lore_gilded_7.name: Etiquette
lore_gilded_7.text: Everything at court is done by rule: who bows how deep, who drinks first, who may sit. Breaking a rule is a statement, and everyone reads it.

lore_person_c_leander.name: Crown Prince Leander
lore_person_c_leander.text: The Crown Prince and your betrothed, correct to the letter, who has never looked at you as if you were a person. Until lately.

lore_person_c_alaric.name: Sir Alaric Thorne
lore_person_c_alaric.text: Knight of the Imperial Guard who walks three paces behind you, has seen everything you did and remembers it.

lore_person_c_dorian.name: Lord Dorian Vael
lore_person_c_dorian.text: Heir of the Duke of Vael, the cleverest man at court and your oldest enemy, who has just noticed you have changed.

lore_person_c_celestine.name: Celestine Aure
lore_person_c_celestine.text: The saint the whole empire adores, the heroine of the story, and far too kind to you for someone you are meant to torment.

lore_person_c_odile.name: Odile Fenn
lore_person_c_odile.text: Your lady’s maid of eight years, who knows where every secret in the palace sleeps and has never once smiled at you.

lore_arena.name: Ice & Arena
lore_arena.about: A cold harbour city that lives for its ice hockey team, the Northgate Wolves. Everyone shares one old arena: the men’s team, the women’s team, the skating club and the press box. The owner is quietly selling up.

lore_arena_1.name: The arena
lore_arena_1.text: The old Northgate arena: a horn that sticks, seats older than the players, and fries the whole city swears by. The tunnel smells of ice and coffee.

lore_arena_2.name: Northgate Wolves
lore_arena_2.text: The city’s ice hockey team, last in the league and loved anyway. Erik Holt captains it; Teddy Novak is the rookie everyone hopes will save it.

lore_arena_3.name: The women’s team
lore_arena_3.text: The Wolves’ women’s side, with the best goalie in the league and the five a.m. ice. Priya Raman is the only reporter who covers it.

lore_arena_4.name: The skating club
lore_arena_4.text: A small skating club that rents the arena’s early ice. Sasha Volkova coaches there, and would like the hockey players to stop ruining her surface.

lore_arena_5.name: The sale
lore_arena_5.text: The owner is quietly selling the team to a buyer who would move it to another city, unless the Wolves make the playoffs and the city fills the seats.

lore_arena_6.name: The rule on the wall
lore_arena_6.text: A sign taped to the treatment room wall: no dating the players. Someone has underlined it twice. Nobody will say who.

lore_arena_7.name: The derby
lore_arena_7.text: The monthly derby against the city across the water, and at the end of the season, the game that decides everything.

lore_person_c_erik.name: Erik Holt
lore_person_c_erik.text: Captain of the Northgate Wolves, scarred, says four words a day, and nobody touches his tape.

lore_person_c_teddy.name: Teddy Novak
lore_person_c_teddy.text: Rookie star of the Wolves, raised on a farm, happy about everything, who turns up at your door with far too much breakfast.

lore_person_c_freya.name: Freya Lund
lore_person_c_freya.text: Goalie of the Wolves women’s team, who shares the five a.m. ice with you and has said maybe nine words so far.

lore_person_c_sasha.name: Sasha Volkova
lore_person_c_sasha.text: Figure skater on the arena’s early ice, who hates hockey, hates the cold and has decided she especially hates you.

lore_person_c_priya.name: Priya Raman
lore_person_c_priya.text: Sports columnist with a story, a press pass and a very good reason to keep flirting with you in the tunnel.

body: Union meeting in an hour, and I already know I will not hear a word of it.
Because last night you said I sound different when I talk to you. Softer. I have been trying to work out if that is a compliment.
I decided it is. I am keeping it.
You walked home in the rain and only told me after. Next time I am calling, and you are picking up.
Also: honey street lights. I looked out the window for ten minutes trying to see what you saw.
First real conversation. You argued back. Nobody argues back.
I think I like that a lot.
The café was too loud and I did not mind at all.
I hummed the new chorus under the table and you were the only one who noticed. It has your name on it now, in my head at least.
Rehearsal ran until two. Your message was the last thing I read before sleep.
A thousand years of skies in the archive, and tonight I wrote down a new one.
You asked which star I would give you. I have not answered yet. It is a serious question and deserves the right star.

d_1.title: Rain on the way home
d_1.body: Missed the bus and walked the whole way. Somehow it was not bad at all - the street lights on the wet road looked like someone spilled honey.

reply.text: You walked home in the rain and did not even text me? Next time call. I will keep you company the whole way.

d_2.title: Exam week
d_2.body: Three chapters down, two to go. I keep rereading the same paragraph. Tomorrow I start earlier, promise.

reply.text: Two chapters is not nothing. Sleep first. I will check on you in the morning.

d_3.title: Cookies
d_3.body: Tried the recipe he described. Burned the first batch. The second one was actually good!

d_4.title: Quiet Sunday
d_4.body: Did nothing. On purpose. Highly recommend.

sn_1.prompt: If the childhood me met the childhood you, would we have been friends?
sn_1.theirNote: Friends? I would have followed you around the playground until you gave up and let me. Six-year-old me was already very persuasive.

sn_2.prompt: What song makes you think of me?
sn_2.theirNote: Any song with rain in it. Because you told me once that rain makes you brave. Now I cannot hear it without thinking of you.
sn_2.myNote: The one you hummed on the live. I still have it on repeat.

greet: Hi. I was hoping it was you.
farewell: Okay. Sleep well - I mean it.
Go rest. I will still be here tomorrow.
Fine, go. Text me the second you wake up.
Good night. Dream about something nice. Maybe me.
answer: Honestly? I was hoping you would ask.
Short answer: yes. Long answer: you will have to call me for that one.
Mostly thinking. About things. About you, a little.
You really want to know? Okay - no laughing.
I was literally thinking about you. Creepy timing.

happy: Okay, that actually made me smile.
See? This is why I like talking to you.
playful: Oh? Bold of you to say that to me.
Mm, I will pretend I did not enjoy that.
You are trouble, you know that.
shy: You cannot just say things like that...
Ah. Okay. Give me a second.
tender: I like hearing about your day, even the small parts.
worried: Hey... that does not sound okay.
Wait, slow down. I am here.
sad: I was hoping you would stay longer.
annoyed: That is all I get. Noted.

comfort: Hey. Slow down. I am right here.
You do not have to carry it alone. I mean that.
Breathe for a second. I am not going anywhere.
tease: You say that like I will not remember it later.
Careful. I might start thinking you like me.
Is this you flirting? Because it is working. A little.
You know I drop everything when you text me. Do not let it go to your head.

Seaside Academy: The vending machine ate my coins again. I am taking it personally.
Someone asked why I was smiling at my phone in the lecture. I lied.
I walked past the sea on the way back and thought of you.
Moonlit Realm: The castle was so quiet tonight I could hear the candles burn.
I found an old map in the library. One corner is marked with a moon nobody can explain.
The night guard caught me smiling at nothing. I blamed the stars.
NEON TIDE: Rehearsal ran three hours over. My legs are jelly.
I hummed a new melody all day. It sounds a bit like you.
The manager took my phone for an hour. Worst hour of the day.
Tidepool Café: A regular left a tip with a little drawing of a cat. Made my whole shift.
I burned the first batch of scones today. Do not tell anyone.
It rained all afternoon, so the café smelled like coffee and wet umbrellas.
Velvet District: It has been raining for three days. The whole city smells like wet matches.
Someone at the Orchid asked about you tonight. I said I had never heard of you.
I walked the long way home and thought about what you said.
Gilded Empire: Three people bowed to me today and two of them meant it. A good day, by court standards.
The Empress’s tea was too sweet, and so was everyone’s smile. I thought of you.
I found a note in my glove this morning. Nobody will say who put it there.
Ice & Arena: The horn stuck again at practice. It went off for a full minute. Nobody even looked up.
I got a bruise the shape of a small country today. You would be impressed.
The ice was perfect this morning and I thought, you should see this.
default: I almost texted you earlier, then got shy about it.
I found a song this morning that sounds like you.
Today was slow. Then you texted, so it got better.

followUp: Okay, but what did you do after?
careAsk: What happened? Start from the beginning.
Do you want to talk about it, or should I distract you?
Is it the kind of bad where you want company, or quiet?

ask: Okay, new question: what is the best thing you ate this week?
Random, but - if we had a free day tomorrow, where would you take me?
What is one small thing that made you smile today?
tell: Okay, I am changing the subject. You owe me one good story from this week.
New rule: tomorrow you tell me the best thing you ate this week.

ask: Hey, I remembered something you told me: "{m}". Still true?
